at gabe.explanation: "At gabe" means "to yawn". It also describes a big opening. For example, "Hullet gaber" (The hole gapes).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke lade være med at **gabe**, når jeg er træt.
sentence.en: I cannot help yawning when I am tired.

at gange.explanation: "At gange" means "to multiply". To say you multiply numbers, say: "Jeg ganger to med tre" (I multiply two by three). It comes from "gange" (times). For example, "Tre gange to er seks" (Three times two is six).

sentence.da: I skolen lærer vi at **gange** og dividere.
sentence.en: At school we learn to multiply and divide.

at garantere.explanation: "At garantere" means "to guarantee". To say you guarantee something, say: "Jeg garanterer, at den virker" (I guarantee that it works). To say you promise to do something, use "at love" (to promise): "Jeg lover at komme" (I promise to come).

sentence.da: Butikken vil **garantere**, at varen kan sendes tilbage inden for tredive dage.
sentence.en: The store will guarantee that the item can be sent back within thirty days.

at gemme.explanation: "At gemme" means "to save", as in saving a file. For example, "Husk at gemme filen" (Remember to save the file). To put something where nobody finds it, it means "to hide": "Hun gemte nøglen" (She hid the key).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gemme** billedet på min telefon.
sentence.en: I want to save the picture on my phone.

at gemme sig.explanation: "At gemme sig" means "to hide (oneself)". The small word "sig" must go with it and changes to "mig" for "I". For example, "Jeg gemmer mig bag døren" (I hide behind the door). To save a file, use "at gemme" without "sig": "Jeg gemmer filen" (I save the file).

sentence.da: Katten plejer at **gemme sig** under sengen.
sentence.en: The cat usually hides under the bed.

at genbruge.explanation: "At genbruge" means "to recycle or reuse". The part "gen-" means "again", so it is "at bruge" (to use) again.

sentence.da: Papir og glas kan man **genbruge**.
sentence.en: Paper and glass can be recycled.

at generalisere.explanation: "At generalisere" means "to generalize". To tell someone they are claiming something about everyone after seeing only a few cases, say: "Du generaliserer for meget" (You are generalizing too much).

sentence.da: Man kan ikke **generalisere** ud fra kun to eksempler.
sentence.en: You cannot generalize from only two examples.

at genere.explanation: "At genere" means "to bother". To check that you are not in someone's way, ask: "Generer jeg dig?" (Am I bothering you?)

sentence.da: Musikken kan **genere** naboerne om natten.
sentence.en: The music can bother the neighbors at night.

at gengive.explanation: "At gengive" means "to reproduce or render". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at give" (to give). To say a picture shows a scene, use it for pictures too: "Maleriet gengiver en storm" (The painting shows a storm).

sentence.da: En god journalist skal **gengive** politikerens ord præcist.
sentence.en: A good journalist must reproduce the politician's words exactly.

at genkende.explanation: "At genkende" means "to recognize". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at kende" (to know), so you know someone again. To say you do not know who a person is, say: "Jeg genkender ham ikke" (I do not recognize him).

sentence.da: Kan du **genkende** manden på billedet?
sentence.en: Can you recognize the man in the picture?

at gennemføre.explanation: "At gennemføre" means "to carry out". It is built from "gennem" (through) and "at føre" (to lead), so you lead something through to the end. To say someone finished a course of study, say: "Hun har gennemført uddannelsen" (She has completed the degree program).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **gennemføre** planen og bygge en ny skole.
sentence.en: The municipality will carry out the plan and build a new school.

at gennemgå.explanation: "At gennemgå" means "to go through or review". To say you look at a text point by point, say: "Vi gennemgår kontrakten" (We go through the contract). To say someone lived through something hard, use it for that too: "Hun har gennemgået en stor operation" (She has been through a major operation).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **gennemgå** opgaverne med klassen i morgen.
sentence.en: The teacher will go through the exercises with the class tomorrow.

at gennemskue.explanation: "At gennemskue" means "to see through", as in understanding a trick, not looking through glass. To say you understood a lie, say: "Jeg gennemskuede hans løgn" (I saw through his lie).

sentence.da: Politiet kunne hurtigt **gennemskue** svindlerens plan.
sentence.en: The police could quickly see through the swindler's plan.

at genopbygge.explanation: "At genopbygge" means "to rebuild". The part "gen-" means "again", as in "at genstarte" (to restart). To say a city was built up again after a war, say: "Byen blev genopbygget efter krigen" (The city was rebuilt after the war).

sentence.da: Efter branden vil de **genopbygge** huset på samme sted.
sentence.en: After the fire they will rebuild the house in the same place.

at genoplive.explanation: "At genoplive" means "to revive". The part "gen-" means "again", as in "at genskabe" (to recreate). To say you bring an old custom back into use, say: "Vi vil genoplive den gamle tradition" (We want to revive the old tradition).

sentence.da: Lægen forsøgte at **genoplive** manden efter hjertestoppet.
sentence.en: The doctor tried to revive the man after the cardiac arrest.

at genoprette.explanation: "At genoprette" means "to restore". To say a lost connection is working again, say: "Vi har genoprettet forbindelsen" (We have restored the connection). For an old building or painting, use "at restaurere" (to restore): "De restaurerer maleriet" (They are restoring the painting).

sentence.da: Politiet skal **genoprette** roen efter urolighederne.
sentence.en: The police must restore calm after the riots.

at genoptage.explanation: "At genoptage" means "to resume". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at optage" (to take up). To say someone started work again, say: "Hun har genoptaget sit arbejde" (She has resumed her work).

sentence.da: Vi vil **genoptage** mødet efter frokost.
sentence.en: We will resume the meeting after lunch.

at genoverveje.explanation: "At genoverveje" means "to reconsider". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at overveje" (to consider). To ask someone to think again about a choice, say: "Vil du ikke genoverveje det?" (Won't you reconsider?)

sentence.da: Jeg vil **genoverveje** tilbuddet og svare dig i morgen.
sentence.en: I will reconsider the offer and answer you tomorrow.

at genskabe.explanation: "At genskabe" means "to recreate or restore". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at skabe" (to create). To say you cannot make an error happen again, say: "Vi kan ikke genskabe fejlen" (We cannot reproduce the error).

sentence.da: Forskerne kunne ikke **genskabe** resultatet i deres eget laboratorium.
sentence.en: The researchers could not recreate the result in their own laboratory.

at genstarte.explanation: "At genstarte" means "to restart". To give advice about a router, say: "Prøv at genstarte routeren" (Try restarting the router). To say a company starts a business activity again, say: "Firmaet genstarter produktionen" (The company restarts production).

sentence.da: Hvis skærmen fryser, kan du **genstarte** computeren.
sentence.en: If the screen freezes, you can restart the computer.

at gentage.explanation: "At gentage" means "to repeat". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "at tage" (to take). To say that something happens again, add "sig" (itself): "Historien gentager sig" (History repeats itself).

sentence.da: Kan du **gentage** det langsomt, tak?
sentence.en: Can you repeat that slowly, please?

at gide.explanation: "At gide" means "to bother or can be bothered". To say you have no energy or wish to do something, say: "Jeg gider ikke" (I can't be bothered). To ask whether someone feels like joining, ask: "Gider du komme med?" (Do you feel like coming along?)

sentence.da: Han vil nok ikke **gide** at hjælpe os.
sentence.en: He probably won't feel like helping us.

at gifte sig.explanation: "At gifte sig" means "to get married". The small word "sig" must go with it and changes to match who marries. For example, "du gifter dig" (you get married) and "han gifter sig" (he gets married). To say what state you are in, use "gift" (married): "Jeg er gift" (I am married).

sentence.da: De vil **gifte sig** i kirken.
sentence.en: They want to get married in the church.

at give.explanation: "At give" means "to give". To ask someone to pass you something at the table, say: "Giv mig saltet, tak" (Pass me the salt, please). To say you do not stop trying, use "at give op" (to give up): "Jeg giver ikke op" (I am not giving up).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give** dig en gave.
sentence.en: I want to give you a present.

at give afkald på.explanation: "At give afkald på" means "to give up or renounce". The small word "på" (on) must come right before the thing you give up. For example, "Hun gav afkald på sin løn" (She gave up her pay).

sentence.da: Man kan **give afkald på** sin arv og lade andre få den.
sentence.en: You can renounce your inheritance and let others get it.

at give besked.explanation: "At give besked" means "to let someone know". To be the one who is told, use "at få besked" (to be notified): "Jeg fik besked i går" (I was notified yesterday).

sentence.da: Kan du **give besked**, når du er fremme?
sentence.en: Can you let me know when you arrive?

at give efter.explanation: "At give efter" means "to give in". To say that a thing broke under weight, use it for things too: "Isen gav efter" (The ice gave way).

sentence.da: Forældrene vil ikke **give efter**, selv om barnet græder.
sentence.en: The parents will not give in, even though the child is crying.

at give en hånd med.explanation: "At give en hånd med" means "to give a hand". To ask for help with a job, say: "Kan du give en hånd med?" (Can you lend a hand?) The word "med" (along) shows that you join in on a job someone is already doing.

forms.da: jeg har givet en hånd med

sentence.da: Vi vil gerne **give en hånd med** flytningen.
sentence.en: We would like to give a hand with the move.

at give lov.explanation: "At give lov" means "to give permission". To say a parent allowed something, say: "Min mor gav lov" (My mother gave permission). The word "lov" also means "law", as in "en ny lov" (a new law).

sentence.da: Far vil nok **give lov**, når vi spørger pænt.
sentence.en: Dad will probably give permission when we ask nicely.

at give op.explanation: "At give op" means "to give up". To tell someone not to quit, say: "Giv ikke op!" (Do not give up!) The small word "op" (up) is in many phrases, such as "at skrive op" (to write down) and "at ringe op" (to call up).

sentence.da: Det er svært, men jeg vil ikke **give op**.
sentence.en: It is hard, but I won't give up.

at give sig.explanation: "At give sig" means "to give in or yield". To say you will not back down, say: "Jeg giver mig ikke" (I will not back down). To say pain eases off, use it for pain too: "Smerterne giver sig" (The pain eases off).

sentence.da: Hun vil ikke **give sig**, før hun har fået et svar.
sentence.en: She will not back down until she has an answer.

at give tilbage.explanation: "At give tilbage" means "to give back". To ask for your own thing back, say: "Giv mig bogen tilbage" (Give me the book back). To bring something back to a shop or library, use "at returnere" (to return): "Jeg returnerer bogen" (I am returning the book).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **give tilbage**, hvad jeg har lånt.
sentence.en: I want to give back what I borrowed.

at glemme.explanation: "At glemme" means "to forget". To say you forgot to bring something, say: "Jeg glemte mine nøgler" (I forgot my keys). To say you forgot to do something, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Jeg glemte at ringe" (I forgot to call).

sentence.da: Jeg må ikke **glemme** min paraply.
sentence.en: I must not forget my umbrella.

at glide.explanation: "At glide" means "to slide or slip". To say something slipped by accident, say: "Kniven gled" (The knife slipped).

sentence.da: Skøjteløberen kan **glide** hen over isen uden at anstrenge sig.
sentence.en: The skater can glide across the ice without any effort.

at glo.explanation: "At glo" means "to stare". It is a blunt word, not a polite one. To challenge someone who is staring at you, say: "Hvad glor du på?" (What are you staring at?)

sentence.da: Det er uhøfligt at **glo** på folk.
sentence.en: It is rude to stare at people.

at glæde.explanation: "At glæde" means "to please or delight". To say news makes you happy, say: "Det glæder mig at høre det" (I am pleased to hear that). Do not mix it up with "at glæde sig til" (to look forward to), where "sig" (oneself) makes you the one who feels it. For example, "Jeg glæder mig til ferien" (I look forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Det vil **glæde** mormor meget at se dig.
sentence.en: It will please grandma a lot to see you.

at glæde sig over.explanation: "At glæde sig over" means "to be happy about". To say you are happy about something that is already here, say: "Han glæder sig over de gode nyheder" (He is happy about the good news). For something in the future, use "at glæde sig til" (to look forward to): "Jeg glæder mig til ferien" (I look forward to the vacation).

sentence.da: Hun kan **glæde sig over** de små ting i livet.
sentence.en: She can be happy about the small things in life.

at glæde sig til.explanation: "At glæde sig til" means "to look forward to". The small word "sig" changes with the person. For example, "Vi glæder os til festen" (We look forward to the party). For something that is already here, use "at glæde sig over" (to be happy about): "Hun glæder sig over resultatet" (She is happy about the result).

sentence.da: Børnene begynder at **glæde sig til** sommerferien.
sentence.en: The children are starting to look forward to the summer vacation.

at gløde.explanation: "At gløde" means "to glow". To say a person is full of a strong feeling, use it for people too: "Hun gløder af stolthed" (She glows with pride).

sentence.da: Jernet skal **gløde**, før smeden kan forme det.
sentence.en: The iron must glow before the smith can shape it.

at gnave.explanation: "At gnave" means "to gnaw". To say a worry keeps bothering you, use it for thoughts too: "Tanken gnavede i mig" (The thought gnawed at me).

sentence.da: Hunden vil **gnave** på knoglen hele dagen.
sentence.en: The dog wants to gnaw on the bone all day.

at gnide.explanation: "At gnide" means "to rub". To say you rub cream into your skin, add "ind" (in): "at gnide creme ind" (to rub in cream).

sentence.da: Hun må **gnide** sine kolde hænder for at få varmen.
sentence.en: She has to rub her cold hands to get warm.

at godkende.explanation: "At godkende" means "to approve". It is built from "god" (good) and "at kende" (to know). To say a plan has been approved, say: "De har godkendt planen" (They have approved the plan).

sentence.da: Chefen skal **godkende** budgettet, før vi bruger penge.
sentence.en: The boss has to approve the budget before we spend money.

at godtage.explanation: "At godtage" means "to accept". It is built from "god" (good) and "at tage" (to take). To say you do not take an excuse as good enough, say: "Skolen godtager ikke den undskyldning" (The school does not accept that excuse).

sentence.da: Vi kan ikke **godtage** den høje pris.
sentence.en: We cannot accept the high price.

at google.explanation: "At google" means "to google". To say you will look something up right away, say: "Jeg googler det lige" (I will just google it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **google** en opskrift på pandekager.
sentence.en: I want to google a recipe for pancakes.

at grave.explanation: "At grave" means "to dig". To say something is dug out of the ground, add "op" (up): "Hunden graver en knogle op" (The dog digs up a bone).

sentence.da: Med en spade kan man **grave** et dybt hul.
sentence.en: With a spade you can dig a deep hole.

at gribe.explanation: "At gribe" means "to grab or catch". To say someone took hold of something with the hand, say: "Han greb min arm" (He grabbed my arm).

sentence.da: Kan du **gribe** bolden, når jeg kaster den?
sentence.en: Can you catch the ball when I throw it?

at gribe ind.explanation: "At gribe ind" means "to intervene". It is built from "at gribe" (to grab) and "ind" (in), as if you reach into the situation. To say someone stepped in to stop a problem, say: "Politiet greb ind" (The police stepped in).

sentence.da: Læreren må **gribe ind**, når børnene begynder at slås.
sentence.en: The teacher has to intervene when the children start fighting.

at grille.explanation: "At grille" means "to grill". To say you are grilling without naming the food, say: "Vi griller i aften" (We are grilling tonight).

sentence.da: Vi kan **grille** pølser i haven, når det er varmt.
sentence.en: We can grill sausages in the garden when it is warm.

at grine.explanation: "At grine" means "to laugh". To say you laughed, say: "Vi grinede meget" (We laughed a lot). To say who you laugh at, add "af" (at): "Hvorfor griner du af mig?" (Why are you laughing at me?)

sentence.da: Børnene vil **grine** af den sjove klovn.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny clown.

at gro.explanation: "At gro" means "to grow", as in plants coming up from the ground. To say plants come up, say: "Græsset gror" (The grass is growing). For a child getting taller or something getting bigger, use "at vokse" (to grow bigger): "Barnet vokser" (The child is growing).

sentence.da: Tomater kan **gro** i et drivhus, når det er koldt ude.
sentence.en: Tomatoes can grow in a greenhouse when it is cold outside.

at gruble.explanation: "At gruble" means "to brood or ponder". To say someone sits and thinks for a long time, say: "Han sidder og grubler" (He is sitting there brooding).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ligge vågen og **gruble** over mine problemer.
sentence.en: I can lie awake and brood over my problems.

at gruppere.explanation: "At gruppere" means "to group". It comes from the noun "en gruppe" (a group). To say you put things into groups, say: "Jeg grupperer billederne i mapper" (I group the pictures into folders).

sentence.da: Læreren vil **gruppere** eleverne efter niveau.
sentence.en: The teacher will group the students by level.

at græde.explanation: "At græde" means "to cry", as in weeping. To ask someone why they are crying, say: "Hvorfor græder du?" (Why are you crying?) To say what made you cry, add "af" (from): "Jeg græd af glæde" (I cried with joy).

sentence.da: Barnet er ked af det og vil **græde**.
sentence.en: The child is sad and wants to cry.

at gynge.explanation: "At gynge" means "to swing". To say a boat moves gently on the water, say: "Båden gynger på bølgerne" (The boat sways on the waves). To swing a club, use "at svinge" (to swing): "Han svinger køllen" (He swings the club).

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at **gynge** på legepladsen.
sentence.en: The children love to swing at the playground.

at gå.explanation: "At gå" means "to go or walk". To say you are leaving, say: "Jeg går nu" (I am leaving now). To say how things are going, say: "Det går godt" (It is going well). To say a bus runs, say: "Bussen går hver time" (The bus runs every hour). To go by car, use "at køre" (to drive): "Vi kører til Aarhus" (We drive to Aarhus).

sentence.da: Vi vil hellere **gå** end køre.
sentence.en: We would rather walk than drive.

at gå af.explanation: "At gå af" means "to resign or go off". To say someone gives up a post, say: "Hun går af som formand" (She resigns as chair). To say you leave a bus or train, say: "Jeg går af ved næste stop" (I get off at the next stop). To say an alarm clock rings, say: "Alarmen gik af" (The alarm went off).

sentence.da: Direktøren vil **gå af**, når året er slut.
sentence.en: The director will resign when the year is over.

at gå agurk.explanation: "At gå agurk" means "to go crazy". Literally, it is "to go cucumber" ("en agurk" is a cucumber). To tell someone they are driving you crazy, say: "Du får mig til at gå agurk!" (You are driving me crazy!)

forms.da: Jeg er ved at gå agurk
forms.en: I am about to go crazy

sentence.da: Jeg kan **gå agurk**, når børnene larmer hele dagen.
sentence.en: I could go crazy when the children make noise all day.

at gå amok.explanation: "At gå amok" means "to go berserk". To say a person lost control in anger, say: "Han gik amok på kontoret" (He went berserk in the office).

sentence.da: Tyren kan **gå amok** og løbe ind i folkemængden.
sentence.en: The bull can go berserk and run into the crowd.

at gå en tur.explanation: "At gå en tur" means "to go for a walk". To say where you walk, add the place after it: "gå en tur i parken" (go for a walk in the park). The words "en tur" also mean "a trip", as in "en tur til Aarhus" (a trip to Aarhus).

forms.en: I have been for a walk

sentence.da: Efter maden vil vi **gå en tur**.
sentence.en: After the meal we want to go for a walk.

at gå forbi.explanation: "At gå forbi" means "to pass by". The small word "forbi" (past) goes with other verbs too. For example, "Bilen kører forbi" (The car drives past).

sentence.da: Jeg plejer at **gå forbi** bageren på vej hjem.
sentence.en: I usually pass the bakery on the way home.

at gå fra hinanden.explanation: "At gå fra hinanden" means "to break up". Literally, it is "to go from each other", and "hinanden" means "each other". To say a couple separated, say: "Mine forældre gik fra hinanden, da jeg var ti" (My parents split up when I was ten).

sentence.da: Efter tre år besluttede de at **gå fra hinanden**.
sentence.en: After three years they decided to break up.

at gå galt.explanation: "At gå galt" means "to go wrong". To say a plan failed, say: "Planen gik galt" (The plan went wrong). To say an answer is wrong, use "forkert" (wrong): "Svaret er forkert" (The answer is wrong).

sentence.da: Det kan **gå galt**, når vejen er glat.
sentence.en: It can go wrong when the road is slippery.

at gå glip af.explanation: "At gå glip af" means "to miss out on". To say you did not get to be part of an event, say: "Hun gik glip af festen" (She missed out on the party). To say you were too late for a bus, use "at misse" (to miss): "Jeg missede bussen" (I missed the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **gå glip af** koncerten.
sentence.en: I don't want to miss out on the concert.

at gå hjem.explanation: "At gå hjem" means "to go home". To go home by car, use "at køre hjem" (to drive home): "Vi kører hjem" (We drive home). To go home by any means, use "at tage hjem" (to head home): "Jeg tager hjem nu" (I am heading home now).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **gå hjem**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to go home.

at gå i biografen.explanation: "At gå i biografen" means "to go to the movies". Literally, it is "to go in the movie theater". To suggest it in a shorter way, say: "Skal vi gå i bio?" (Shall we go to the movies?)

forms.en: I have gone to the movies

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå i biografen** i aften.
sentence.en: We want to go to the movies tonight.

at gå i gang med.explanation: "At gå i gang med" means "to get started on". The small word "med" (with) goes before the task you start. For example, "Hun gik i gang med maden" (She got started on the food). When no task follows, leave "med" out: "Vi er gået i gang" (We have started).

forms.da: jeg er gået i gang med

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå i gang med** opgaven nu.
sentence.en: We have to get started on the task now.

at gå i panik.explanation: "At gå i panik" means "to panic". Literally, it is "to go into panic". To tell someone to stay calm, use "at bevare roen" (to stay calm): "Bevar roen!" (Stay calm!)

sentence.da: Du skal ikke **gå i panik**, for vi har god tid.
sentence.en: Don't panic, because we have plenty of time.

at gå i seng.explanation: "At gå i seng" means "to go to bed". Falling asleep is different, so use "at falde i søvn" (to fall asleep): "Jeg faldt i søvn i sofaen" (I fell asleep on the sofa).

sentence.da: Børnene er trætte og skal **gå i seng**.
sentence.en: The children are tired and have to go to bed.

at gå i stykker.explanation: "At gå i stykker" means "to break". To say your phone stopped working, say: "Min telefon gik i stykker" (My phone broke). To say you broke something yourself, use "at ødelægge" (to ruin): "Jeg ødelagde telefonen" (I ruined the phone).

sentence.da: Den gamle cykel kan nemt **gå i stykker**.
sentence.en: The old bike can easily break.

at gå i stå.explanation: "At gå i stå" means "to come to a standstill". To say a machine stopped working, say: "Maskinen gik i stå" (The machine stopped). To say your mind went blank, say: "Jeg gik helt i stå" (My mind went completely blank).

forms.en: it has come to a standstill

sentence.da: Arbejdet kan **gå i stå**, når pengene slipper op.
sentence.en: The work can come to a standstill when the money runs out.

at gå igennem.explanation: "At gå igennem" means "to go through". To say you walk from one side of a place to the other, say: "Vi gik igennem skoven" (We went through the forest). To say you go over something step by step, put the thing before "igennem": "Vi går opgaven igennem" (We go over the task).

sentence.da: Vi kan **gå igennem** tunnelen til den anden side.
sentence.en: We can go through the tunnel to the other side.

at gå ind.explanation: "At gå ind" means "to go in". The small word "ind" (in) is for going in. For example, "Hun går ind i butikken" (She walks into the shop). To say someone is already inside, use "inde" (inside): "Han er inde i huset" (He is inside the house).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ind** i huset nu.
sentence.en: We have to go into the house now.

at gå ind for.explanation: "At gå ind for" means "to be in favor of". To say you back an idea, say: "De går ind for flere cykelstier" (They are in favor of more bike lanes). To say you are against something, use "at gå imod" (to go against): "Jeg går imod forslaget" (I am against the proposal).

forms.en: I have been in favor of

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gå ind for** forslaget, hvis prisen er rimelig.
sentence.en: I will support the proposal if the price is reasonable.

at gå med til.explanation: "At gå med til" means "to agree to". The small word "til" (to) comes before what you agree to: "Jeg går med til forslaget" (I agree to the proposal).

sentence.da: Han ville ikke **gå med til** at sælge huset.
sentence.en: He did not want to agree to sell the house.

at gå ned.explanation: "At gå ned" means "to go down". To say the sun sets, use it for the sun: "Solen går ned" (The sun sets). To say you go down to a lower floor, say: "Jeg går ned i kælderen" (I go down to the basement).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå ned** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk down the stairs.

at gå op.explanation: "At gå op" means "to go up". To say the sun rises, use it for the sun: "Solen går op" (The sun rises). To say a sum comes out right, say: "Regnestykket går op" (The sum adds up).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gå op** ad trappen.
sentence.en: We have to walk up the stairs.

at gå op for.explanation: "At gå op for" means "to dawn on". To say who realizes something, put that person after "for": "Det gik op for mig, at jeg tog fejl" (It dawned on me that I was wrong).

forms.da: det er gået op for mig

sentence.da: Det vil snart **gå op for** dig, hvor svært det er.
sentence.en: It will soon dawn on you how hard it is.

at gå over åen efter vand.explanation: "At gå over åen efter vand" means "to make things unnecessarily complicated". Literally, it is "to go over the stream for water", as if you cross a stream to fetch water when there is water close by.

forms.da: Du går over åen efter vand
forms.en: You are making things unnecessarily complicated

forms.da: Lad os ikke gå over åen efter vand
Hvorfor gå over åen efter vand?
forms.en: Why take the long way round?

related.da: at gøre en myg til en elefant
related.en: to make a mountain out of a molehill

sentence.da: Det er dumt at **gå over åen efter vand**, når løsningen er nem.
sentence.en: It is silly to make things unnecessarily complicated when the solution is easy.

at gå på café.explanation: "At gå på café" means "to go to a café". Danish says "på café" (literally, "on café") with no "en" (a) in front of "café". To suggest it to a friend, say: "Skal vi gå på café?" (Shall we go to a café?)

forms.en: I have gone to a café

related.en: to go out on the town

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå på café** i dag.
sentence.en: We want to go to a café today.

at gå på nerverne.explanation: "At gå på nerverne" means "to get on someone's nerves". Literally, it is "to go on the nerves". To name the person who is annoyed, put that person right after "går" (goes): "Larmen går mig på nerverne" (The noise gets on my nerves).

forms.da: jeg er gået ham på nerverne
forms.en: I have gotten on his nerves

sentence.da: Lyden fra en dryppende vandhane kan **gå på nerverne**.
sentence.en: The sound of a dripping faucet can get on your nerves.

at gå på pension.explanation: "At gå på pension" means "to retire". The word "pension" also means the money paid to a person who has retired. For example, "Han får pension" (He gets a pension).

sentence.da: Min far vil **gå på pension**, når han bliver 67.
sentence.en: My father will retire when he turns 67.

at gå rundt.explanation: "At gå rundt" means "to walk around". To say you walk around a place, add "om" (around) before the place: "Vi gik rundt om søen" (We walked around the lake). The small word "rundt" (around) goes with other verbs too. For example, "Børnene løber rundt" (The children run around).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **gå rundt** og se på butikkerne.
sentence.en: I would like to walk around and look at the stores.

at gå som katten om den varme grød.explanation: "At gå som katten om den varme grød" means "to beat around the bush". Literally, it is "to go like the cat around the hot porridge", a picture of a cat circling food that is too hot to eat.

forms.da: Du går som katten om den varme grød
forms.en: You are beating around the bush

forms.da: Gå ikke som katten om den varme grød
forms.en: Do not beat around the bush

forms.da: Hun gik som katten om den varme grød

sentence.da: Han vil **gå som katten om den varme grød** i stedet for at svare.
sentence.en: He wants to beat around the bush instead of answering.

at gå som smurt.explanation: "At gå som smurt" means "to go smoothly". Literally, it is "to go like greased", and "smurt" comes from "at smøre" (to grease). To say a plan worked without trouble, say: "Alt gik som smurt" (Everything went smoothly).

sentence.da: Hvis vi forbereder os godt, vil prøven **gå som smurt**.
sentence.en: If we prepare well, the test will go smoothly.

at gå tabt.explanation: "At gå tabt" means "to be lost". To say a letter disappeared, say: "Brevet gik tabt" (The letter was lost). To say you lost something yourself, use "at miste" (to lose): "Jeg mistede min nøgle" (I lost my key).

sentence.da: Hvis computeren går i stykker, kan data **gå tabt**.
sentence.en: If the computer breaks, data can be lost.

at gå til.explanation: "At gå til" means "to go to (regularly)". To say you attend a hobby or class regularly, say: "Jeg går til svømning" (I go to swimming lessons). To ask how something happened, use the question: "Hvordan gik det til?" (How did that happen?)

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gå til** fodbold, ligesom sin storebror.
sentence.en: He would like to play soccer, just like his big brother.

at gå til eksamen.explanation: "At gå til eksamen" means "to take an exam". To say when you sit it, say: "Hun går til eksamen i morgen" (She takes an exam tomorrow). To say you study for it, use "at læse til eksamen" (to study for an exam): "Jeg læser til eksamen" (I am studying for the exam).

sentence.da: Jeg har læst meget, og nu skal jeg **gå til eksamen**.
sentence.en: I have studied a lot, and now I have to take the exam.

at gå tilbage.explanation: "At gå tilbage" means "to go back". To drive back, use "at køre tilbage" (to drive back): "Vi kører tilbage i morgen" (We drive back tomorrow). To say numbers are falling, use it for that too: "Salget går tilbage" (Sales are going down).

sentence.da: Nu skal vi **gå tilbage** til stationen.
sentence.en: Now we have to walk back to the station.

at gå ud.explanation: "At gå ud" means "to go out". To ask someone to go out for the evening, say: "Skal vi gå ud i aften?" (Shall we go out tonight?) To say a light stopped shining, say: "Lyset gik ud" (The light went out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **gå ud** i haven nu.
sentence.en: We want to go out into the garden now.

at gå ud fra.explanation: "At gå ud fra" means "to assume". The words "ud fra" also mean "based on" in other sentences. For example, "Ud fra tallene ser det godt ud" (Based on the numbers, it looks good).

sentence.da: Vi må **gå ud fra**, at han kommer.
sentence.en: We have to assume that he is coming.

at gå ud med.explanation: "At gå ud med" means "to go out with". To say two people are dating, say: "Hun går ud med Peter" (She is going out with Peter). To say you take a dog for a walk, say: "Jeg går ud med hunden" (I am taking the dog out).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gå ud med** hende, fordi han kan lide hende.
sentence.en: He would like to go out with her because he likes her.

at gå videre.explanation: "At gå videre" means "to move on". To say someone has left a past relationship or event behind, say: "Hun er gået videre" (She has moved on).

sentence.da: Efter pausen skal vi **gå videre** til næste emne.
sentence.en: After the break we move on to the next topic.

at gå væk.explanation: "At gå væk" means "to go away". The command "Gå væk!" (Go away!) is a blunt order. To say someone walked off, say: "Han gik væk uden at sige farvel" (He walked off without saying goodbye).

sentence.da: Katten vil **gå væk** fra hunden.
sentence.en: The cat wants to go away from the dog.

at gætte.explanation: "At gætte" means "to guess". To name your guess, add "på" (on): "Jeg gætter på Peter" (I am guessing Peter). To start telling someone surprising news, say: "Gæt hvad!" (Guess what!)

sentence.da: Kan du **gætte** min alder?
sentence.en: Can you guess my age?

at gø.explanation: "At gø" means "to bark". The present form "gør" is spelled exactly like "gør" from "at gøre" (to do). For barking, say: "Hunden gør" (The dog barks). For doing, say: "Jeg gør det" (I do it).

sentence.da: Hunden må ikke **gø** om natten.
sentence.en: The dog is not allowed to bark at night.

at gøre.explanation: "At gøre" means "to do". To avoid repeating a verb, use it in place of that verb: "Jeg læser, og det gør hun også" (I am reading, and she does too). To say you make something, such as food, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver mad" (I am cooking).

sentence.da: Hvad vil du **gøre** i dag?
sentence.en: What do you want to do today?

at gøre det forbi.explanation: "At gøre det forbi" means "to end it (a relationship)". To name the person you ended it with, add "med" (with): "Hun gjorde det forbi med ham" (She ended it with him). To say it with another phrase, use "at slå op" (to break up): "Han slog op med hende" (He broke up with her).

sentence.da: Hun elsker ham ikke mere og vil **gøre det forbi**.
sentence.en: She no longer loves him and wants to end it.

at gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden.explanation: "At gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden" means "to make a virtue of necessity". In it, "en dyd" means "a virtue" and "nødvendigheden" means "the necessity".

forms.da: Han gør en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: He makes a virtue of necessity

forms.da: Hun gjorde en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: She made a virtue of necessity

forms.da: Vi må gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden
forms.en: We have to make a virtue of necessity

related.da: at gøre det bedste ud af det
related.en: to make the best of it

related.da: at gøre gode miner til slet spil
related.en: to put on a brave face

related.da: at bide i det sure æble

sentence.da: Vi har ikke råd til ferie og må **gøre en dyd af nødvendigheden**.
sentence.en: We cannot afford a vacation and must make a virtue of necessity.

at gøre en forskel.explanation: "At gøre en forskel" means "to make a difference". To describe the size of the difference, put a word such as "stor" (big) before "forskel" (difference): "at gøre en stor forskel" (to make a big difference).

sentence.da: Et smil kan **gøre en forskel** for en ensom person.
sentence.en: A smile can make a difference for a lonely person.

at gøre færdig.explanation: "At gøre færdig" means "to finish". To say you finish a task, say: "Jeg gør opgaven færdig" (I am finishing the assignment). To say you are done yourself, use "at blive færdig" (to be done): "Jeg bliver færdig klokken fem" (I will be done at five).

sentence.da: Lad mig lige **gøre færdig**, og så kommer jeg.
sentence.en: Let me just finish, and then I will come.

at gøre grin med.explanation: "At gøre grin med" means "to make fun of". The small word "med" (with) goes before the person you make fun of. For example, "Hun gør grin med mig" (She makes fun of me).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **gøre grin med** andre.
sentence.en: You should not make fun of others.

at gøre indtryk.explanation: "At gøre indtryk" means "to make an impression". To say who was affected, add "på" (on) before that person: "Filmen gjorde stort indtryk på mig" (The film made a big impression on me).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne **gøre indtryk** på sine nye kolleger.
sentence.en: He wants to make an impression on his new colleagues.

at gøre klar.explanation: "At gøre klar" means "to get ready". To say you prepare something, say: "Jeg gør maden klar" (I am getting the food ready). To say you prepare yourself, add "mig" (myself): "Jeg gør mig klar" (I am getting myself ready).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **gøre klar** til festen.
sentence.en: I have to get ready for the party.

at gøre noget ved.explanation: "At gøre noget ved" means "to do something about". To tell someone to act, say: "Gør noget!" (Do something!) To say what you act on, put it after "ved": "Jeg vil gøre noget ved støjen" (I want to do something about the noise).

sentence.da: Vi må **gøre noget ved** det nu.
sentence.en: We have to do something about it now.

at gøre ondt.explanation: "At gøre ondt" means "to hurt". To say which body part hurts, put the body part first: "Min fod gør ondt" (My foot hurts). To say where you have pain, use "have ondt i" (have pain in): "Jeg har ondt i maven" (I have a stomachache).

sentence.da: Det kan **gøre ondt** at falde på isen.
sentence.en: It can hurt to fall on the ice.

at gøre rent.explanation: "At gøre rent" means "to clean", literally "to make clean". To say you clean a room, put the room between "gør" (make) and "rent" (clean): "Jeg gør køkkenet rent" (I clean the kitchen).

sentence.da: Vi skal **gøre rent** i huset.
sentence.en: We have to clean the house.

at gøre sig umage.explanation: "At gøre sig umage" means "to make an effort". The word "sig" (oneself) changes with the person. For example, "Jeg gør mig umage" (I make an effort), "Du gør dig umage" (You make an effort). To name what you put the effort into, add "med" (with): "Hun gør sig umage med maden" (She makes an effort with the food).

sentence.da: Eleverne vil **gøre sig umage** med opgaven.
sentence.en: The students will make an effort with the assignment.

at gøre sit bedste.explanation: "At gøre sit bedste" means "to do one's best". The word "sit" (one's) changes with who does it. For example, "Han gør sit bedste" (He does his best), "Jeg gør mit bedste" (I do my best).

sentence.da: Hver elev skal **gøre sit bedste** til prøven.
sentence.en: Each student must do their best for the test.

en gaben.explanation: "En gaben" means "a yawn". It is built from the verb "at gabe" (to yawn). To say you yawn in class, use the verb: "Jeg gaber i timen" (I yawn in class).

sentence.da: Han skjulte sin **gaben** bag hånden.
sentence.en: He hid his yawn behind his hand.

en gade.explanation: "En gade" means "a street". To say children play in the street, use "på gaden" (in the street): "Børnene leger på gaden" (The children play in the street). To talk about a road between towns, use "en vej" (a road): "Vejen til Odense er lang" (The road to Odense is long).

sentence.da: Vi går ned ad en **gade** med huse.
sentence.en: We walk down a street with houses.

en gadedør.explanation: "En gadedør" means "a street door". It is built from "gade" (street) and "dør" (door). The part "dør" is spelled the same as the verb "dør" (dies). For example, "Fuglen dør" (The bird dies).

sentence.da: Huset har en blå **gadedør** ud til gaden.
sentence.en: The house has a blue street door facing the street.

en gadekat.explanation: "En gadekat" means "a stray cat". It is built from "gade" (street) and "kat" (cat). To talk about a cat that lives with a family, use "en huskat" (a house cat): "Vi har en huskat" (We have a house cat).

sentence.da: En **gadekat** bor ude og har ingen ejer.
sentence.en: A stray cat lives outside and has no owner.

en gadelygte.explanation: "En gadelygte" means "a streetlight". It is built from "gade" (street) and "lygte" (lantern).

sentence.da: Om natten lyser en **gadelygte** gaden op.
sentence.en: At night, a streetlight lights up the street.

en gaffel.explanation: "En gaffel" means "a fork". A very common phrase is "kniv og gaffel" (knife and fork). For example, "Jeg spiser med kniv og gaffel" (I eat with a knife and fork).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser maden med en **gaffel**.
sentence.en: I eat the food with a fork.

en galakse.explanation: "En galakse" means "a galaxy". The galaxy that our sun is in is called "Mælkevejen" (the Milky Way), literally "the milk road".

sentence.da: Vores sol ligger i en **galakse**, som hedder Mælkevejen.
sentence.en: Our sun lies in a galaxy called the Milky Way.

en gallerist.explanation: "En gallerist" means "a gallery owner". It is built from "et galleri" (a gallery) and the ending "-ist", which names a person.

sentence.da: Hun er **gallerist** og sælger malerier for unge kunstnere.
sentence.en: She is a gallery owner and sells paintings for young artists.

en galning.explanation: "En galning" means "a madman". It comes from the adjective "gal" (mad). To say someone drives wildly, use "som en galning" (like a madman): "Han kører som en galning" (He drives like a madman).

sentence.da: Kun en **galning** kører hundrede kilometer i timen i byen.
sentence.en: Only a madman drives a hundred kilometers an hour in town.

en gang.explanation: "En gang" means "a hallway". To say how many times something happens, the same word means "time": "Jeg har været der to gange" (I have been there two times).

sentence.da: Der er mange døre i den lange **gang**.
sentence.en: There are many doors in the long hallway.

en gang imellem.explanation: "En gang imellem" means "once in a while". It is built from "en gang" (one time) and "imellem" (between). To say you do something from time to time, use it in the sentence: "Jeg ringer til min bror en gang imellem" (I call my brother once in a while).

forms.da: Jeg ser dem en gang imellem.
forms.en: I see them once in a while.
once in a while in the summer

forms.da: Vi spiser ude en gang imellem.
forms.en: We eat out once in a while.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser pizza **en gang imellem**.
sentence.en: I eat pizza once in a while.

en gang om ugen.explanation: "En gang om ugen" means "once a week". To say how many times, change the number: "tre gange om ugen" (three times a week). To name a different period, change the last word: "en gang om dagen" (once a day).

sentence.da: Jeg træner **en gang om ugen**.
sentence.en: I work out once a week.

en garage.explanation: "En garage" means "a garage". To say where the car is, use "i" (in): "Bilen står i garagen" (The car is in the garage).

sentence.da: Vi har en **garage** til bilen.
sentence.en: We have a garage for the car.

en garanti.explanation: "En garanti" means "a warranty". When you give a personal promise, the same word means "a guarantee": "Der er ingen garanti for det" (There is no guarantee of that).

sentence.da: Der er to års **garanti** på computeren.
sentence.en: The computer has a two-year warranty.

en gartner.explanation: "En gartner" means "a gardener". A place where a gardener grows plants to sell is "et gartneri" (a plant nursery). For example, "Vi køber tomater fra gartneriet" (We buy tomatoes from the plant nursery).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **gartner** og passer planter i parken.
sentence.en: My neighbor is a gardener and takes care of plants in the park.

en gate.explanation: "En gate" means "a gate", as at an airport where you board a plane. To talk about a gate in a garden, use "en låge" (a garden gate): "Haven har en grøn låge" (The garden has a green gate).

sentence.da: Flyet til Rom går fra **gate** tolv.
sentence.en: The plane to Rome leaves from gate twelve.

en gaveindpakning.explanation: "En gaveindpakning" means "a gift wrapping". It is built from "en gave" (a present) and "en indpakning" (a wrapping). To ask a shop to wrap a present, say: "Kan I pakke gaven ind?" (Can you wrap the present?)

sentence.da: Butikken tilbyder gratis **gaveindpakning**.
sentence.en: The shop offers free gift wrapping.

en ged.explanation: "En ged" means "a goat". It is also in "gedeost" (goat cheese), built from "ged" and "ost" (cheese). For example, "Jeg vil have gedeost på salaten" (I want goat cheese on the salad).

sentence.da: En **ged** spiser græs og giver mælk.
sentence.en: A goat eats grass and gives milk.

en gedde.explanation: "En gedde" means "a pike". To say you fish for pike, use "fiske efter" (fish for): "Vi fisker efter gedder i søen" (We fish for pike in the lake).

sentence.da: En **gedde** er en rovfisk med skarpe tænder i søen.
sentence.en: A pike is a predatory fish with sharp teeth in the lake.

en genbrugsbutik.explanation: "En genbrugsbutik" means "a secondhand shop". It is built from "genbrug" (recycling) and "en butik" (a shop). To talk about a place for old furniture, do not use it; use "en genbrugsstation" (a recycling center): "Vi kører gamle møbler til genbrugsstationen" (We drive old furniture to the recycling center).

sentence.da: I en **genbrugsbutik** er tøjet brugt og billigt.
sentence.en: In a secondhand shop the clothes are used and cheap.

en genbrugsstation.explanation: "En genbrugsstation" means "a recycling center". It is built from "genbrug" (recycling) and "en station" (a station). To say where you take old furniture, say: "Vi kører gamle møbler til genbrugsstationen" (We drive old furniture to the recycling center).

sentence.da: Man sorterer sit affald på en **genbrugsstation**.
sentence.en: You sort your waste at a recycling center.

en general.explanation: "En general" means "a general". The same word starts "en generalprøve" (a dress rehearsal). For example, "Vi har generalprøve i morgen" (We have the dress rehearsal tomorrow).

sentence.da: En **general** er den højeste officer i hæren.
sentence.en: A general is the highest officer in the army.

en generation.explanation: "En generation" means "a generation". To count the steps in a family, put a number in front and use the plural: "Tre generationer bor i huset" (Three generations live in the house).

sentence.da: Børn og deres forældre er ikke af samme **generation**.
sentence.en: Children and their parents are not of the same generation.

en generationskløft.explanation: "En generationskløft" means "a generation gap". It is built from "en generation" (a generation) and "en kløft" (a ravine). The word "kløft" alone also names a gap between two groups. For example, "Der er en kløft mellem rig og fattig" (There is a gap between rich and poor).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **generationskløft** mellem mine bedsteforældre og mig.
sentence.en: There is a big generation gap between my grandparents and me.

en gennemgang.explanation: "En gennemgang" means "a review or walkthrough". It is built from "gennem" (through) and "en gang" (a passage). On a sign, it means a path through a place. For example, "Gennemgang forbudt" (No passage).

sentence.da: Læreren laver en **gennemgang** af reglerne, før prøven starter.
sentence.en: The teacher goes over the rules before the test starts.

en gennemsnitsløn.explanation: "En gennemsnitsløn" means "an average salary". It is built from "et gennemsnit" (an average) and "en løn" (pay). To say "on average", use "i gennemsnit": "I gennemsnit sover jeg otte timer" (On average I sleep eight hours).

sentence.da: En **gennemsnitsløn** er summen af alle lønninger delt med antallet af personer.
sentence.en: An average salary is the sum of all salaries divided by the number of people.

en genopretning.explanation: "En genopretning" means "a recovery", as in an economy or order being restored. It comes from the verb "at genoprette" (to restore). To say a person recovers from an illness, use "at komme sig" (to get better): "Han er ved at komme sig efter sygdommen" (He is recovering from the illness).

sentence.da: Regeringen arbejder på en **genopretning** af landets økonomi.
sentence.en: The government is working on a recovery of the country's economy.

en genre.explanation: "En genre" means "a genre". To ask what kind of music someone likes, say: "Hvilken genre kan du bedst lide?" (Which genre do you like best?)

sentence.da: Rock er en **genre** inden for musik.
sentence.en: Rock is a genre within music.

en genstand.explanation: "En genstand" means "an object". To name an object nobody can identify, say: "en ukendt genstand" (an unidentified object). To say a person is the target of something, use "genstand for" (object of): "Hun er genstand for kritik" (She is the object of criticism).

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en mærkelig **genstand** i haven.
sentence.en: The police found a strange object in the garden.

en genstart.explanation: "En genstart" means "a restart". The beginning "gen-" means "again", as in "at genbruge" (to reuse). To tell someone to restart a device, use the verb "at genstarte": "Prøv at genstarte routeren" (Try restarting the router).

sentence.da: Hvis telefonen hænger, kan en **genstart** ofte løse problemet.
sentence.en: If the phone freezes, a restart can often solve the problem.

en genvej.explanation: "En genvej" means "a shortcut". The last part, "vej", means "road". To say you take a shortcut, use "tage" (take): "Vi tager genvejen over marken" (We take the shortcut across the field). On a computer, a key combination is called "en tastaturgenvej" (a keyboard shortcut).

sentence.da: Vi tog en **genvej** og kom hurtigt hjem.
sentence.en: We took a shortcut and got home quickly.

en gerning.explanation: "En gerning" means "a deed". A common phrase is "i ord og gerning" (in word and deed). For example, "Hun hjælper både i ord og gerning" (She helps in both word and deed).

sentence.da: En god **gerning** er noget, man gør for at hjælpe andre.
sentence.en: A good deed is something you do to help others.

en gerningsmand.explanation: "En gerningsmand" means "a perpetrator". It is built from "en gerning" (a deed) and "en mand" (a man). To say perpetrator without saying man or woman, use "en gerningsperson" (a perpetrator): "Politiet leder efter en gerningsperson" (The police are looking for a perpetrator).

sentence.da: Politiet har fundet den **gerningsmand**, der brød ind i butikken.
sentence.en: The police have found the perpetrator who broke into the store.

en gestus.explanation: "En gestus" means "a gesture", as in a kind act. To talk about a movement of the hand, use "en håndbevægelse" (a hand movement): "Han lavede en håndbevægelse" (He made a hand movement).

sentence.da: Det var en pæn **gestus**, at han bød os på kaffe.
sentence.en: It was a nice gesture that he offered us coffee.

en gevinst.explanation: "En gevinst" means "a prize or winnings". To say something is a benefit for people, the same word means "a gain": "Det er en gevinst for alle" (It is a gain for everyone).

sentence.da: Hun brugte sin **gevinst** fra lotteriet på en rejse.
sentence.en: She spent her prize from the lottery on a trip.

en gift.explanation: "En gift" means "a poison". As an adjective, the same spelling means "married". To say who you are married to, use "gift med" (married to): "Hun er gift med en læge" (She is married to a doctor).

sentence.da: Slangen har en stærk **gift**.
sentence.en: The snake has a strong poison.

sentence.da: En **giraf** har en meget lang hals.
sentence.en: A giraffe has a very long neck.

en gletsjer.explanation: "En gletsjer" means "a glacier". Denmark itself has no glaciers, but Greenland, which belongs to the Danish Realm, has many. To say a glacier is melting, use "smelte" (melt): "Gletsjeren smelter" (The glacier is melting).

sentence.da: En **gletsjer** flytter sig langsomt ned ad bjerget.
sentence.en: A glacier moves slowly down the mountain.

en globus.explanation: "En globus" means "a globe". To show the world on a flat sheet, use "et kort" (a map): "Jeg finder Danmark på et kort" (I find Denmark on a map).

sentence.da: På en **globus** ser man hele jorden.
sentence.en: On a globe you see the whole Earth.

en gnist.explanation: "En gnist" means "a spark". To say a small beginning of a feeling, use "en gnist af" (a spark of): "en gnist af håb" (a spark of hope).

sentence.da: Når man slår to sten mod hinanden, kan der komme en **gnist**.
sentence.en: When you strike two stones together, a spark can appear.

en godkendelse.explanation: "En godkendelse" means "an approval". It comes from the verb "at godkende" (to approve). To say you ask for approval, use "søge om" (apply for): "Vi søger om godkendelse af planen" (We apply for approval of the plan).

sentence.da: Før butikken åbner, skal den have en **godkendelse** fra kommunen.
sentence.en: Before the shop opens, it must have an approval from the municipality.

en godtgørelse.explanation: "En godtgørelse" means "a reimbursement". It comes from the verb "at godtgøre" (to make good). To talk about money for driving your own car for work, put "kørsel" (driving) in front: "Firmaet betaler kørselsgodtgørelse" (The company pays a mileage allowance).

sentence.da: Jeg får **godtgørelse** for benzinen, når jeg kører for arbejdet.
sentence.en: I get reimbursement for the gas when I drive for work.

en gorilla.explanation: "En gorilla" means "a gorilla". The group it belongs to is "menneskeaber" (great apes), literally "human apes". For example, "Gorillaen er en menneskeabe" (The gorilla is a great ape).

sentence.da: Den store **gorilla** spiser blade og frugt.
sentence.en: The big gorilla eats leaves and fruit.

en grad.explanation: "En grad" means "a degree". To say how warm it is outside, use the plural: "ti grader" (ten degrees). To give the size of an angle, say: "en vinkel på 90 grader" (an angle of 90 degrees). To name a level of university study, say: "en akademisk grad" (an academic degree).

sentence.da: Det er kun én **grad** ude i dag.
sentence.en: It is only one degree outside today.

en graf.explanation: "En graf" means "a graph". To say someone draws one, use "tegne" (draw): "Læreren tegner en graf på tavlen" (The teacher draws a graph on the board).

sentence.da: På en **graf** kan man se, hvordan prisen stiger hver måned.
sentence.en: On a graph you can see how the price rises every month.

en grammatik.explanation: "En grammatik" means "a grammar". It is also the start of "en grammatikbog" (a grammar book), with "en bog" (a book) added. For example, "Jeg læser i en grammatikbog" (I read in a grammar book).

sentence.da: Jeg øver reglerne i dansk **grammatik**.
sentence.en: I practice the rules of Danish grammar.

en gran.explanation: "En gran" means "a spruce or fir". To name one kind of fir, use "en nordmannsgran" (a Nordmann fir): "Vi har en nordmannsgran i stuen" (We have a Nordmann fir in the living room).

sentence.da: En **gran** har nåle og er grøn hele vinteren.
sentence.en: A spruce has needles and is green all winter.

en granat.explanation: "En granat" means "a grenade". Do not mix it up with "et granatæble" (a pomegranate), which is built from "granat" and "et æble" (an apple). For example, "Jeg spiser et granatæble" (I eat a pomegranate).

sentence.da: En **granat** eksploderer kort efter, at splitten er trukket ud.
sentence.en: A grenade explodes shortly after the pin is pulled out.

en gratisavis.explanation: "En gratisavis" means "a free newspaper". It is built from "gratis" (free) and "en avis" (a newspaper).

sentence.da: En **gratisavis** koster ingenting, fordi reklamerne betaler for den.
sentence.en: A free newspaper costs nothing because the ads pay for it.

en grav.explanation: "En grav" means "a grave". The same word also names a long ditch dug in the ground, as in "en voldgrav" (a moat).

sentence.da: Efter begravelsen ligger den døde i en **grav** på kirkegården.
sentence.en: After the funeral the dead person lies in a grave in the cemetery.

en graviditet.explanation: "En graviditet" means "a pregnancy". It is built from "gravid" (pregnant). To say a woman is pregnant, say: "Hun er gravid" (She is pregnant).

sentence.da: Under en **graviditet** vokser barnet i moderens mave.
sentence.en: During a pregnancy the baby grows in the mother's belly.

en graviditetstest.explanation: "En graviditetstest" means "a pregnancy test". It is built from "graviditet" (pregnancy) and "en test" (a test). To say you do one, use "tage" (take): "Jeg tager en graviditetstest" (I take a pregnancy test).

sentence.da: Med en **graviditetstest** kan man selv se, om man er gravid.
sentence.en: With a pregnancy test you can see for yourself whether you are pregnant.

en gravko.explanation: "En gravko" means "an excavator". It is built on the verb "at grave" (to dig).

sentence.da: En **gravko** graver et stort hul.
sentence.en: An excavator digs a big hole.

en gravsten.explanation: "En gravsten" means "a gravestone". It is built from "en grav" (a grave) and "en sten" (a stone). To say you lay flowers there, say: "Jeg lægger blomster ved gravstenen" (I lay flowers at the gravestone).

sentence.da: På en **gravsten** står den dødes navn og fødselsår.
sentence.en: On a gravestone you find the dead person's name and birth year.

en gren.explanation: "En gren" means "a branch", as in a tree. To talk about a small thin branch, use "en kvist" (a twig): "Der ligger en kvist på stien" (There is a twig on the path).

sentence.da: Fuglen sidder på en **gren** i træet.
sentence.en: The bird sits on a branch in the tree.

en grill.explanation: "En grill" means "a grill". The matching verb is "at grille" (to grill). To say what you grill, put the food after the verb: "Vi griller pølser" (We grill sausages).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad ude på en **grill**.
sentence.en: We cook outside on a grill.

en grillbar.explanation: "En grillbar" means "a grill bar". It is built from "en grill" (a grill) and "en bar" (a bar).

sentence.da: På en **grillbar** kan man købe burgere og pølser med pommes frites.
sentence.en: At a grill bar you can buy burgers and sausages with fries.

en grillfest.explanation: "En grillfest" means "a barbecue party". It is built from "en grill" (a grill) and "en fest" (a party). To say you are barbecuing, use the verb "at grille" (to grill): "Vi griller i aften" (We are barbecuing tonight).

sentence.da: Til en **grillfest** spiser vi pølser og salat.
sentence.en: At a barbecue party we eat sausages and salad.

en grimasse.explanation: "En grimasse" means "a grimace". To say someone pulls faces, use "at skære grimasser" (to pull faces), where "skære" otherwise means "to cut": "Børnene skærer grimasser" (The children are pulling faces).

sentence.da: Han lavede en **grimasse**, fordi citronen var meget sur.
sentence.en: He made a grimace because the lemon was very sour.

en gris.explanation: "En gris" means "a pig". Said about a person, it is rude. For example, "Du er en gris!" (You are a pig!)

sentence.da: Jeg ser en lyserød **gris** på gården.
sentence.en: I see a pink pig on the farm.

en grund.explanation: "En grund" means "a reason". To say "for that reason", use "af den grund": "Han var syg, og af den grund blev han hjemme" (He was ill, and for that reason he stayed home). To say a plot of land, the same word is used: "Vi køber en grund og bygger et hus" (We buy a plot of land and build a house).

sentence.da: Der er ingen **grund** til at være bange.
sentence.en: There is no reason to be afraid.

en grundlov.explanation: "En grundlov" means "a constitution". It is built from "grund" (base) and "en lov" (a law). In Denmark, 5 June is "Grundlovsdag" (Constitution Day).

sentence.da: I en **grundlov** står der, hvilke rettigheder borgerne har.
sentence.en: A constitution states which rights the citizens have.

en grundskole.explanation: "En grundskole" means "a primary school". In Denmark it covers ten years, from 0th grade to 9th grade, not just the first years.

sentence.da: Danske børn går i **grundskole** i ti år.
sentence.en: Danish children attend primary school for ten years.

en gruppe.explanation: "En gruppe" means "a group". To say what the group is made of, put the word right after "gruppe", with no word for "of": "en gruppe børn" (a group of children).

sentence.da: Vi arbejder i en **gruppe** på fire.
sentence.en: We work in a group of four.

en gryde.explanation: "En gryde" means "a pot". To say what is in the pot, put the food right after "gryde": "Vi laver en gryde suppe" (We make a pot of soup). To talk about the pan for frying, use "en pande" (a pan): "Jeg steger æg på en pande" (I fry eggs in a pan).

sentence.da: Jeg koger kartofler i en stor **gryde**.
sentence.en: I boil potatoes in a big pot.

en grydelap.explanation: "En grydelap" means "a pot holder". It is built from "en gryde" (a pot) and "en lap" (a piece of cloth).

sentence.da: Jeg tager brødet ud af ovnen med en **grydelap**.
sentence.en: I take the bread out of the oven with a pot holder.

en grænse.explanation: "En grænse" means "a border". Denmark's only land border is the one with Germany. For example, "grænsen til Tyskland" (the border with Germany). To talk about a limit, the same word is used: "Alt har en grænse" (Everything has a limit).

sentence.da: Ved en **grænse** skal du vise dit pas.
sentence.en: At a border you must show your passport.

en grænseværdi.explanation: "En grænseværdi" means "a limit value". It is built from "grænse" (limit) and "en værdi" (a value). To say the limit is passed, use "overskride" (exceed): "Vandet overskrider grænseværdien" (The water exceeds the limit value).

sentence.da: Der er en **grænseværdi** for, hvor meget støj en fabrik må lave.
sentence.en: There is a limit value for how much noise a factory may make.

en græshoppe.explanation: "En græshoppe" means "a grasshopper". The first part of the word is "græs" (grass).

sentence.da: En **græshoppe** kan hoppe langt, fordi dens bagben er stærke.
sentence.en: A grasshopper can jump far because its back legs are strong.

en græsslåmaskine.explanation: "En græsslåmaskine" means "a lawnmower". It is built from "græs" (grass), "at slå" (to mow) and "en maskine" (a machine). The verb "slå" normally means "to hit", so "at slå græs" is literally "to hit grass". For example, "Jeg slår græsset" (I mow the grass).

sentence.da: Græsset er højt, og jeg henter min **græsslåmaskine**.
sentence.en: The grass is tall, and I am getting my lawnmower.

en græsslåning.explanation: "En græsslåning" means "a lawn mowing". It is built from "græs" (grass) and the verb "at slå" (to mow). The verb "slå" normally means "to hit". For example, "Jeg slår græs i dag" (I mow the grass today).

sentence.da: Efter en times **græsslåning** er plænen pæn og kort.
sentence.en: After an hour of lawn mowing, the lawn is neat and short.

en grævling.explanation: "En grævling" means "a badger". To name the home it digs in the ground, use "en grævlingegrav" (a badger sett): "Vi fandt en grævlingegrav i skoven" (We found a badger sett in the forest).

sentence.da: En **grævling** bor i et hul i skoven og sover om dagen.
sentence.en: A badger lives in a hole in the forest and sleeps during the day.

en grønlænder.explanation: "En grønlænder" means "a Greenlander". Greenland, "Grønland", is part of the Danish Realm. To name the language, use "grønlandsk" (Greenlandic): "Bogen er skrevet på grønlandsk" (The book is written in Greenlandic).

sentence.da: En **grønlænder** kommer fra Grønland og taler grønlandsk.
sentence.en: A Greenlander comes from Greenland and speaks Greenlandic.

en grønthandler.explanation: "En grønthandler" means "a greengrocer". It is built from "grønt" (vegetables) and "en handler" (a dealer). To talk about the shop, the same word is used: "Jeg går hen til grønthandleren" (I am going over to the greengrocer's).

sentence.da: Jeg køber æbler og gulerødder hos en **grønthandler**.
sentence.en: I buy apples and carrots at a greengrocer's.

en grøntsag.explanation: "En grøntsag" means "a vegetable". It is built from "grønt" (greens) and "en sag" (a thing). To say you eat vegetables, say: "Jeg spiser grøntsager hver dag" (I eat vegetables every day).

sentence.da: En gulerod er en **grøntsag**.
sentence.en: A carrot is a vegetable.

en gud.explanation: "En gud" means "a god". To talk about the one God, say "Gud" without "en": "Tror du på Gud?" (Do you believe in God?)

sentence.da: Thor var en **gud** i gamle dage.
sentence.en: Thor was a god in the old days.

en gudfar.explanation: "En gudfar" means "a godfather". It is built from "gud" (god) and "far" (father). To say whose godfather he is, use "til" (to): "Han er gudfar til min søn" (He is godfather to my son).

sentence.da: Min **gudfar** er min fars bedste ven.
sentence.en: My godfather is my dad's best friend.

en gudmor.explanation: "En gudmor" means "a godmother". It is built from "gud" (god) and "mor" (mother). To say whose godmother she is, use "til" (to): "Hun er gudmor til min datter" (She is godmother to my daughter).

sentence.da: Min **gudmor** er min mors bedste veninde.
sentence.en: My godmother is my mom's best friend.

en guide.explanation: "En guide" means "a guide". To say a tour has a guide, use "guidet" (guided): "Vi tager på en guidet tur" (We go on a guided tour).

sentence.da: Vores **guide** viser os den gamle by.
sentence.en: Our guide shows us the old town.

en guidebog.explanation: "En guidebog" means "a guidebook". It is built from "en guide" (a guide) and "en bog" (a book). To name the place a guidebook covers, use "til" (to): "en guidebog til København" (a guidebook to Copenhagen).

sentence.da: Jeg læser en **guidebog** før turen.
sentence.en: I read a guidebook before the trip.

en guirlande.explanation: "En guirlande" means "a garland". The spelling "guirlande" has "ui" after the "g". To say you hang garlands up, use "hænge op" (hang up): "Vi hænger guirlander op til festen" (We hang garlands up for the party).

sentence.da: Til festen hænger der en **guirlande** af papir over bordet.
sentence.en: For the party there is a paper garland hanging over the table.

en guitar.explanation: "En guitar" means "a guitar". To say an electric one, put "el-" in front: "en elguitar" (an electric guitar).

sentence.da: Min bror spiller **guitar** i et band.
sentence.en: My brother plays guitar in a band.

en guldfisk.explanation: "En guldfisk" means "a goldfish". It is built from "guld" (gold) and "fisk" (fish). The plural stays "guldfisk". For example, "to guldfisk" (two goldfish).

sentence.da: Der svømmer en **guldfisk** rundt i en skål.
sentence.en: A goldfish is swimming around in a bowl.

en guldsmed.explanation: "En guldsmed" means "a dragonfly". When you talk about a person who works with gold, the same word means "a goldsmith": "Ringen er lavet af en guldsmed" (The ring was made by a goldsmith).

sentence.da: Over søen flyver en **guldsmed** med gennemsigtige vinger.
sentence.en: Over the lake flies a dragonfly with transparent wings.

en gulerod.explanation: "En gulerod" means "a carrot". It is built from "gul" (yellow) and "rod" (root), so it is literally "a yellow root". In the plural the vowel changes. For example, "gulerødder" (carrots), as in "Jeg køber tre gulerødder" (I buy three carrots).

sentence.da: Kaninen spiser en orange **gulerod**.
sentence.en: The rabbit eats an orange carrot.

en gulvvask.explanation: "En gulvvask" means "a floor washing". It is built from "gulv" (floor) and "vask" (washing), so both "v" letters stay in the spelling. To say you wash the floor, use the verb: "Jeg vasker gulv hver lørdag" (I wash the floor every Saturday).

sentence.da: En **gulvvask** med varmt vand og sæbe tager kun ti minutter.
sentence.en: A floor washing with hot water and soap takes only ten minutes.

en gummistøvle.explanation: "En gummistøvle" means "a rubber boot". It is built from "gummi" (rubber) and "en støvle" (a boot). To say a pair, use "et par" (a pair of): "et par gummistøvler" (a pair of rubber boots).

sentence.da: Han mistede en **gummistøvle** i mudderet.
sentence.en: He lost a rubber boot in the mud.

en gut.explanation: "En gut" means "a guy or lad". It is an informal word. To greet a group of friends, say: "Hej, gutter!" (Hi, guys!)

sentence.da: Han er en flink **gut**, som altid hjælper sine venner.
sentence.en: He is a nice lad who always helps his friends.

en guvernør.explanation: "En guvernør" means "a governor". To say which place the governor leads, use "i" (in): "guvernøren i Californien" (the governor of California).

sentence.da: En **guvernør** leder en amerikansk delstat.
sentence.en: A governor leads an American state.

en gyde.explanation: "En gyde" means "an alley". To say you walk through an alley, use "gennem" (through): "Vi går gennem gyden" (We walk through the alley).

sentence.da: Den smalle **gyde** mellem husene er næsten mørk.
sentence.en: The narrow alley between the houses is almost dark.

en gymnastiksal.explanation: "En gymnastiksal" means "a school gym". It is built from "gymnastik" (gymnastics) and "en sal" (a hall). The part "sal" is also in "en festsal" (a banquet hall).

sentence.da: Børnene har idræt i skolens **gymnastiksal**, når det regner.
sentence.en: The children have PE in the school gym when it rains.

en gynge.explanation: "En gynge" means "a swing", as at a playground. To say a child is swinging, use the verb "at gynge" (to swing): "Barnet gynger" (The child is swinging).

sentence.da: Far skubber mig på en **gynge**.
sentence.en: Dad pushes me on a swing.

en gåde.explanation: "En gåde" means "a riddle or mystery". To say you solve a riddle by guessing, use "gætte" (guess): "Kan du gætte gåden?" (Can you guess the riddle?) When nobody can explain something, the same word means "a mystery": "Det er en gåde, hvorfor hun forsvandt" (It is a mystery why she disappeared).

sentence.da: Børnene prøver at løse en **gåde** i bogen.
sentence.en: The children try to solve a riddle in the book.

en gågade.explanation: "En gågade" means "a pedestrian street". It is built from "gå" (walk) and "en gade" (a street).

sentence.da: Ingen biler må køre i en **gågade**.
sentence.en: Cars may not drive in a pedestrian street.

en gård.explanation: "En gård" means "a farm or a courtyard". When you talk about the shared yard behind an apartment building, the same word means "a courtyard": "Børnene leger i gården" (The children play in the courtyard).

sentence.da: Vi besøger en **gård** og ser køer og grise.
sentence.en: We visit a farm and see cows and pigs.

en gårdhave.explanation: "En gårdhave" means "a courtyard garden". It is built from "gård" (courtyard) and "have" (garden). The first part, "gård", also means "a farm". For example, "Vi bor på en gård" (We live on a farm).

sentence.da: Der er en lille **gårdhave** med blomster bag huset.
sentence.en: There is a small courtyard garden with flowers behind the house.

en gås.explanation: "En gås" means "a goose". The dish is called "gåsesteg" (roast goose), built from "gås" plus "steg" (roast). In Denmark, many families eat roast duck or goose on 10 November, which is "Mortens aften" (St. Martin's Eve).

sentence.da: En **gås** er en stor fugl og bor ved vandet.
sentence.en: A goose is a big bird and lives by the water.

en gåtur.explanation: "En gåtur" means "a walk". It is built from "at gå" (to walk) and "en tur" (a trip). To say you are going for a walk, say: "Jeg går en tur" (I am going for a walk).

sentence.da: Vi tager på **gåtur** i skoven.
sentence.en: We go for a walk in the forest.

en gæld.explanation: "En gæld" means "a debt". To say someone owes nothing, say: "Hun har ingen gæld" (She has no debt). To say you finish paying a debt, say: "Vi betaler gælden af" (We pay off the debt).

sentence.da: Efter huskøbet har de **gæld** til banken.
sentence.en: After buying the house, they have debt to the bank.

en gæst.explanation: "En gæst" means "a guest". To say visitors are coming to your home, say: "Vi får gæster" (We are having guests). A guest at a hotel is "en hotelgæst" (a hotel guest).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad til vores **gæst**.
sentence.en: We cook for our guest.

en gætteleg.explanation: "En gætteleg" means "a guessing game". It is built from "at gætte" (to guess) and "en leg" (a game). The part "leg" also appears in "at lege" (to play). For example, "Børnene leger" (The children are playing).

sentence.da: I en **gætteleg** skal du gætte svaret.
sentence.en: In a guessing game, you have to guess the answer.

et gab.explanation: "Et gab" means "a yawn". The same word also names the wide open jaws of a big animal. To say a lion's jaws, say: "løvens gab" (the lion's jaws).

sentence.da: Han skjuler et **gab** bag hånden, fordi mødet er så langt.
sentence.en: He hides a yawn behind his hand because the meeting is so long.

et gadekryds.explanation: "Et gadekryds" means "an intersection". It is built from "en gade" (a street) and "et kryds" (a cross). The part "kryds" also means a cross mark. To ask someone to mark a spot, say: "Sæt et kryds her" (Put a cross here).

sentence.da: Drej til højre ved næste **gadekryds**.
sentence.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

et galleri.explanation: "Et galleri" means "a gallery". English speakers should spell it with "-i" at the end, not "-y": "galleri".

sentence.da: Vi ser på kunst i et lille **galleri**.
sentence.en: We look at art in a small gallery.

et gardin.explanation: "Et gardin" means "a curtain". To say you close the curtains, say: "Hun trækker gardinerne for" (She closes the curtains). To say you open them, use "fra" instead of "for": "Hun trækker gardinerne fra" (She opens the curtains).

sentence.da: Et **gardin** hænger foran vinduet og holder lyset ude.
sentence.en: A curtain hangs in front of the window and keeps the light out.

et gavekort.explanation: "Et gavekort" means "a gift card". It is built from "en gave" (a gift) and "et kort" (a card). To say you give someone a gift card, say: "Jeg giver hende et gavekort" (I give her a gift card).

sentence.da: Med et **gavekort** kan man købe ting.
sentence.en: With a gift card you can buy things.

et gear.explanation: "Et gear" means "a gear". To say you move to a lower gear on a hill, say: "Jeg skifter ned" (I shift down). To move to a higher gear, say "skifte op" (shift up).

sentence.da: Jeg skifter **gear**, når vejen går opad.
sentence.en: I shift gears when the road goes uphill.

et gebyr.explanation: "Et gebyr" means "a fee". To name the fee for paying late, use "et rykkergebyr" (a reminder fee). To say you have to pay it, say: "Jeg skal betale et gebyr" (I have to pay a fee).

sentence.da: Banken tager et **gebyr** på halvtreds kroner for hver overførsel.
sentence.en: The bank charges a fee of fifty kroner for each transfer.

et gen.explanation: "Et gen" means "a gene". To say a trait runs in the family, say: "Det ligger i generne" (It runs in the family), literally "It lies in the genes".

sentence.da: Hvert **gen** bærer instruktioner om, hvordan kroppen skal bygges.
sentence.en: Each gene carries instructions about how the body is built.

et geni.explanation: "Et geni" means "a genius". To say what a person is brilliant at, put "i" (in) or "til" (for) and the subject after it: "Hun er et geni i matematik" (She is a genius at math).

sentence.da: Min bror er et **geni** til matematik.
sentence.en: My brother is a genius at math.

et gennembrud.explanation: "Et gennembrud" means "a breakthrough". It is built from "gennem" (through) and "et brud" (a break). To say when an artist became well known, say: "Hendes gennembrud kom i 2010" (Her breakthrough came in 2010).

sentence.da: Efter mange års arbejde fik forskerne endelig et **gennembrud**.
sentence.en: After many years of work, the researchers finally got a breakthrough.

et gennemsnit.explanation: "Et gennemsnit" means "an average". To say something is better than the average, say: "Hendes karakterer er over gennemsnittet" (Her grades are above average).

sentence.da: Jeg sover syv timer i **gennemsnit**.
sentence.en: I sleep seven hours on average.

et gerningssted.explanation: "Et gerningssted" means "a crime scene". It is built from "en gerning" (a deed) and "et sted" (a place). To say the police close off the area, say: "Politiet afspærrer gerningsstedet" (The police cordon off the crime scene).

sentence.da: Det sted, hvor en forbrydelse er sket, kaldes et **gerningssted**.
sentence.en: The place where a crime has happened is called a crime scene.

et gevir.explanation: "Et gevir" means "a set of antlers". The horns of a cow are different and are called "et horn" (a horn). For example, "Koen har to horn" (The cow has two horns).

sentence.da: Hjorten har et stort **gevir** med mange spidser.
sentence.en: The deer has a large set of antlers with many points.

et gevær.explanation: "Et gevær" means "a rifle". A small gun held in one hand is "en pistol" (a pistol). To say someone has one, say: "Han har en pistol" (He has a pistol).

sentence.da: Jægeren sigter omhyggeligt, før han skyder med sit **gevær**.
sentence.en: The hunter aims carefully before he shoots with his rifle.

et gidsel.explanation: "Et gidsel" means "a hostage". To say someone is taken hostage, say: "De tog ham som gidsel" (They took him hostage).

sentence.da: Bankrøveren holder et **gidsel**, og politiet forhandler med ham.
sentence.en: The bank robber is holding a hostage, and the police are negotiating with him.

et glas.explanation: "Et glas" means "a glass", as in a drinking glass. To say a glass of water, put the drink right after "glas", with no word for "of": "et glas vand" (a glass of water). The same word names the material. For example, "Vinduet er lavet af glas" (The window is made of glass).

sentence.da: Man drikker vand af et **glas**.
sentence.en: You drink water from a glass.

et glimt.explanation: "Et glimt" means "a glimpse". The same word also means a brief flash of light. For example, "et glimt af lys" (a flash of light). To say someone has a playful look, say: "Han har et glimt i øjet" (He has a twinkle in his eye).

sentence.da: Hun fik et **glimt** af solen mellem skyerne.
sentence.en: She got a glimpse of the sun between the clouds.

et gram.explanation: "Et gram" means "a gram". The plural is the same word. To say how heavy a package is, say: "Pakken vejer 500 gram" (The package weighs 500 grams).

sentence.da: Jeg skal bruge to hundrede **gram** mel.
sentence.en: I need two hundred grams of flour.

et grin.explanation: "Et grin" means "a laugh". It is built from the verb "at grine" (to laugh). For a smile, use "et smil" (a smile): "Hun har et stort smil" (She has a big smile).

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **grin** sammen i går.
sentence.en: We had a good laugh together yesterday.
