et grundlag.explanation: "Et grundlag" means "a basis". To say a plan rests on a solid basis, say: "Planen har et solidt grundlag" (The plan has a solid basis). The Danish constitution is called "Grundloven" (the Constitution), built from "grund" (foundation) and "lov" (law).

sentence.da: Aftalen blev det **grundlag**, som resten af planen byggede på.
sentence.en: The agreement became the basis that the rest of the plan was built on.

et grundstof.explanation: "Et grundstof" means "a chemical element". It is built from "grund" (basic) and "et stof" (a substance). To name an element, say: "Ilt er et grundstof" (Oxygen is a chemical element).

sentence.da: Guld er et **grundstof**, som ikke kan deles i noget enklere.
sentence.en: Gold is an element that cannot be split into anything simpler.

et gudbarn.explanation: "Et gudbarn" means "a godchild". It is built from "gud" (god) and "et barn" (a child). The plural is "gudbørn", with "ø" in the second part. To say whose godchild someone is, say: "Hun er min søsters gudbarn" (She is my sister's godchild).

sentence.da: Mit **gudbarn** fylder fem år i dag.
sentence.en: My godchild turns five today.

et guldbryllup.explanation: "Et guldbryllup" means "a golden wedding anniversary". It is built from "guld" (gold) and "et bryllup" (a wedding). The wedding day itself is "et bryllup". For example, "Vi var til bryllup i lørdags" (We went to a wedding last Saturday).

sentence.da: Mine bedsteforældre har været gift i halvtreds år og holder **guldbryllup**.
sentence.en: My grandparents have been married for fifty years and are celebrating their golden wedding.

et gulv.explanation: "Et gulv" means "a floor". To say something lies on the floor, say: "Bogen ligger på gulvet" (The book is on the floor). For a level of a building, use "en etage" (a story): "Vi bor på anden etage" (We live on the second floor).

sentence.da: Et **gulv** er lavet af træ eller sten.
sentence.en: A floor is made of wood or stone.

et gulvtæppe.explanation: "Et gulvtæppe" means "a carpet". It is built from "et gulv" (a floor) and "et tæppe" (a blanket or rug). To say you vacuum it, say: "Jeg støvsuger gulvtæppet" (I vacuum the carpet).

sentence.da: Vi har et blødt **gulvtæppe** i stuen.
sentence.en: We have a soft carpet in the living room.

et gymnasium.explanation: "Et gymnasium" means "a high school". In Denmark, it is a three-year school that prepares students for university. English speakers may think of a gym, but a gym for exercise is "et fitnesscenter" (a gym). For example, "Jeg træner i et fitnesscenter" (I work out in a gym).

related.en: a primary and lower secondary school

sentence.da: Efter folkeskolen går mange unge på et **gymnasium**.
sentence.en: After primary school, many young people go to a gymnasium.

et gys.explanation: "Et gys" means "a shudder". To say something gave you a shudder, say: "Det gav mig et gys" (It gave me a shudder).

sentence.da: Et **gys** løb ned ad ryggen på mig, da døren gik op.
sentence.en: A shudder ran down my back when the door opened.

et gæsteværelse.explanation: "Et gæsteværelse" means "a guest room". It is built from "en gæst" (a guest) and "et værelse" (a room). The part "gæste" also appears in "en gæstebog" (a guest book). For example, "Skriv i gæstebogen" (Write in the guest book).

sentence.da: Du kan sove i vores **gæsteværelse**.
sentence.en: You can sleep in our guest room.

et gøremål.explanation: "Et gøremål" means "a chore". It comes from the verb "at gøre" (to do). To ask what is on the list for today, say: "Hvad er dagens gøremål?" (What are today's chores?)

sentence.da: Jeg har mange **gøremål** i dag, blandt andet at handle og vaske tøj.
sentence.en: I have many chores today, including shopping and washing clothes.

gal.explanation: "Gal" means "crazy". It takes an "e" in the plural. For example, "gale ideer" (crazy ideas). The form "galt" means "wrong", as in "Noget gik galt" (Something went wrong).

sentence.da: Er du helt **gal**? Det er alt for farligt!
sentence.en: Are you completely crazy? That is far too dangerous!

galskab.explanation: "En galskab" means "a crazy act". It comes from "gal" (crazy). To call something a crazy act, say: "Det er en galskab at gå uden jakke i dag" (It is a crazy act to go without a jacket today).

sentence.da: Det er rent **galskab** at sejle i den storm.
sentence.en: It is pure madness to sail in that storm.

galt.explanation: "Galt" means "wrong", as in "Jeg gjorde noget galt" (I did something wrong). To say something is not bad, use "ikke galt" (not bad): "Det er ikke galt" (It is not bad). The word "gal" is different and means "crazy". For example, "Er du gal?" (Are you crazy?)

sentence.da: Noget er **galt** med min computer.
sentence.en: Something is wrong with my computer.

gammel.explanation: "Gammel" means "old". To ask someone's age, say: "Hvor gammel er du?" (How old are you?) To give your age, say: "Jeg er tredive år gammel" (I am thirty years old).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er 90 år og meget **gammel**.
sentence.en: My grandfather is 90 and very old.

gammeldags.explanation: "Gammeldags" means "old-fashioned". The opposite is "moderne" (modern). To say a kitchen is modern, say: "Vi har et moderne køkken" (We have a modern kitchen).

sentence.da: Min mormor har et **gammeldags** køkken.
sentence.en: My grandmother has an old-fashioned kitchen.

gang.explanation: "Gang" means "a time", as in one occasion. To say something happened twice, say: "to gange" (twice). To ask how many times, say: "Hvor mange gange?" (How many times?) The same word also means a hallway: "Skoene står i gangen" (The shoes are in the hallway). For time on the clock, use "tid" (time): "Jeg har ikke tid" (I do not have time).

sentence.da: Jeg har været i Paris en **gang**.
sentence.en: I have been to Paris once.

ganske.explanation: "Ganske" means "quite". To show it is weaker than "meget" (very), compare: "ganske kold" (quite cold) is less cold than "meget kold" (very cold).

sentence.da: Maden var **ganske** god, men lidt dyr.
sentence.en: The food was quite good, but a little expensive.

ganske vist.explanation: "Ganske vist" means "admittedly". To admit one point and then give the other side with "men" (but), say: "Det er ganske vist dyrt, men det er godt" (It is admittedly expensive, but it is good).

forms.da: Hun kom ganske vist for sent

sentence.da: Bilen er **ganske vist** gammel, men den kører fint.
sentence.en: The car is admittedly old, but it runs fine.

garanteret.explanation: "Garanteret" means "definitely". It comes from "en garanti" (a guarantee). To say you are sure someone will be late, say: "Han kommer garanteret for sent" (He is sure to be late).

sentence.da: Når du øver dig hver dag, bliver du **garanteret** bedre.
sentence.en: When you practice every day, you will definitely get better.

gavepapir.explanation: "Gavepapir" means "wrapping paper". It is built from "en gave" (a gift) and "et papir" (a paper). To say you have run out of it, say: "Vi mangler gavepapir" (We are missing wrapping paper).

sentence.da: Jeg pakker gaven ind i rødt **gavepapir**.
sentence.en: I wrap the gift in red wrapping paper.

gavmild.explanation: "Gavmild" means "generous". To say what someone is generous with, put "med" (with) after it: "Hun er gavmild med sin tid" (She is generous with her time).

sentence.da: Han er **gavmild** og betaler ofte for alle sine venner.
sentence.en: He is generous and often pays for all his friends.

gavmildhed.explanation: "En gavmildhed" means "generosity". It comes from "gavmild" (generous). To say someone showed generosity, say: "Hun viste stor gavmildhed" (She showed great generosity).

sentence.da: Det var et tegn på **gavmildhed**, at han betalte for alle.
sentence.en: It was a sign of generosity that he paid for everyone.

gavn.explanation: "Gavn" means "benefit". To say you get use out of something, say: "Jeg har stor gavn af min cykel" (I get great use out of my bike). To say something helps children, say "til gavn for børn" (for the benefit of children): "Pengene går til gavn for børn" (The money goes to the benefit of children).

forms.en: to get use out of something

sentence.da: Motion er til stor **gavn** for hjertet.
sentence.en: Exercise is of great benefit to the heart.

genbrug.explanation: "Genbrug" means "recycling". It is built from "gen" (again) and "brug" (use). The part "gen" also appears in "at genstarte" (to restart). For example, "Prøv at genstarte routeren" (Try restarting the router). In Denmark, you take things to the recycling center, "en genbrugsstation". For example, "Vi kører på genbrugsstationen" (We are driving to the recycling center).

sentence.da: Gamle flasker kan blive til nye ting ved **genbrug**.
sentence.en: Old bottles can become new things through recycling.

generelt.explanation: "Generelt" means "in general". To say what is true overall but not today, say: "Generelt er bussen til tiden, men i dag var den sen" (In general the bus is on time, but today it was late). The word for "general" before a noun is "generel". For example, "en generel regel" (a general rule).

sentence.da: **Generelt** er det varmt i juli, men ikke altid.
sentence.en: Generally it is warm in July, but not always.

genert.explanation: "Genert" means "shy". To say who you are shy around, use "over for" (towards): "Han er genert over for fremmede" (He is shy around strangers).

sentence.da: Jeg er lidt **genert**, når jeg møder nye folk.
sentence.en: I am a bit shy when I meet new people.

generøs.explanation: "Generøs" means "generous". To say what someone is generous with, put "med" (with) after it: "Hun er generøs med sin tid" (She is generous with her time). The opposite is "nærig" (stingy). For example, "Han er nærig" (He is stingy).

sentence.da: Han er **generøs** og giver gerne penge væk.
sentence.en: He is generous and gladly gives money away.

generøsitet.explanation: "En generøsitet" means "generosity". It comes from "generøs" (generous). To thank someone for giving, say: "Vi takker for din generøsitet" (We thank you for your generosity).

sentence.da: Det er **generøsitet**, når man giver uden at forvente noget.
sentence.en: It is generosity when you give without expecting anything.

genetik.explanation: "Genetik" means "genetics". It comes from "et gen" (a gene). To say a trait is in the genes, say: "Det ligger i genetikken" (It is in the genetics).

sentence.da: Inden for **genetik** studerer man, hvad børn arver fra deres forældre.
sentence.en: In genetics, you study what children inherit from their parents.

genetisk.explanation: "Genetisk" means "genetic". It comes from "genetik" (genetics). To say a trait comes from the parents, say: "Hans øjenfarve er genetisk" (His eye color is genetic).

sentence.da: Sygdommen er **genetisk** og går i arv i familien.
sentence.en: The disease is genetic and runs in the family.

genial.explanation: "Genial" means "brilliant". It comes from "et geni" (a genius). To praise a person, say: "Hun er genial" (She is brilliant).

sentence.da: Det er en **genial** idé, og den virker.
sentence.en: It is a brilliant idea, and it works.

gennem.explanation: "Gennem" means "through". When you talk about time, it means "throughout": "Jeg har boet her gennem mange år" (I have lived here for many years).

sentence.da: Vi går **gennem** parken hjem.
sentence.en: We walk home through the park.

gennemført.explanation: "Gennemført" means "polished". It comes from "at gennemføre" (to carry out). It also means "carried out", as in "Planen blev gennemført" (The plan was carried out).

sentence.da: Koncerten var en **gennemført** oplevelse fra start til slut.
sentence.en: The concert was a polished experience from start to finish.

gennemsigtig.explanation: "Gennemsigtig" means "transparent". It is built from "gennem" (through) and "sigt" (sight). To describe a process that hides nothing, say: "en gennemsigtig proces" (a transparent process).

sentence.da: Ruden er **gennemsigtig**, og man kan se ud igennem den.
sentence.en: The window is transparent, and you can see out through it.

gennemsnitlig.explanation: "Gennemsnitlig" means "average". It comes from "et gennemsnit" (an average). To say a day was ordinary, use "almindelig" (ordinary) instead: "Det var en almindelig dag" (It was an ordinary day).

sentence.da: Det er en **gennemsnitlig** pris, ikke den billigste og ikke den dyreste.
sentence.en: It is an average price, not the cheapest and not the most expensive.

genoptræning.explanation: "Genoptræning" means "rehabilitation". It is built from "gen-" (again) and "træning" (training). The part "gen-" also appears in "at gentage" (to repeat). For example, "Kan du gentage det?" (Can you repeat that?)

sentence.da: Efter operationen går jeg til **genoptræning** i tre måneder.
sentence.en: After the surgery, I go to rehabilitation for three months.

gensidighed.explanation: "Gensidighed" means "mutuality". It comes from "gensidig" (mutual). To say a friendship goes both ways, say: "Der er gensidighed i vores venskab" (There is mutuality in our friendship).

sentence.da: I et godt forhold skal der være **gensidighed**.
sentence.en: In a good relationship, there must be mutuality.

geografi.explanation: "Geografi" means "geography". Spell it with "f", not "ph" as in English: "geografi".

sentence.da: Vi lærer om lande og floder i **geografi**.
sentence.en: We learn about countries and rivers in geography.

gerne.explanation: "Gerne" means "gladly". To ask politely, add it to "vil have". Without it, "Jeg vil have en øl" (I want a beer) sounds blunt. To say you are glad to help, say: "Jeg hjælper dig gerne" (I am glad to help you).

forms.en: I am happy to do that.

sentence.da: Jeg vil **gerne** have en kop te.
sentence.en: I would like a cup of tea.

gerrig.explanation: "Gerrig" means "stingy". To praise someone who is careful with money, use "sparsommelig" (thrifty) instead: "Hun er sparsommelig" (She is thrifty).

sentence.da: Han er så **gerrig**, at han aldrig giver drikkepenge.
sentence.en: He is so stingy that he never gives tips.

gerrighed.explanation: "En gerrighed" means "stinginess". It comes from "gerrig" (stingy). To name being careful with money in a good way, use "sparsommelighed" (thrift): "Sparsommelighed er en dyd" (Thrift is a virtue).

sentence.da: Hans **gerrighed** betød, at familien aldrig fik gaver.
sentence.en: His stinginess meant that the family never got gifts.

gift.explanation: "Gift" means "married". To name the partner, add "med" (with) after "gift". To say people got married, use "blive gift" (to get married): "De blev gift i 2015" (They got married in 2015). The same spelling is also the word for "poison". For example, "Slangen har gift" (The snake has poison).

sentence.da: Jeg er **gift** med Anna.
sentence.en: I am married to Anna.

gin.explanation: "Gin" means "gin". To talk about the drink in general, leave out "en": "Jeg kan ikke lide gin" (I do not like gin). To talk about one serving, use "en": "Hun drikker en gin" (She is drinking a gin).

sentence.da: Hun bestiller en **gin** og tonic i baren.
sentence.en: She orders a gin and tonic at the bar.

glad.explanation: "Glad" means "happy". To name the thing that makes you happy, add "for" (about) after "glad": "Jeg er glad for gaven" (I am happy about the gift).

sentence.da: Drengen smiler og er så **glad**.
sentence.en: The boy smiles and is so happy.

glad for.explanation: "Glad for" means "fond of". With a thing, it means "happy with". For example, "Hun er glad for sin bil" (She is happy with her car). To say you love someone, use "elske" (to love) instead: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you).

forms.da: Hun er glad for sin bil.
forms.en: She is happy with her car.

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **glad for** min lejlighed.
sentence.en: I am very happy with my apartment.

glat.explanation: "Glat" means "smooth". The same word means "slippery". For example, "Isen er glat" (The ice is slippery).

sentence.da: Pas på, gulvet er **glat**.
sentence.en: Be careful, the floor is slippery.

glimrende.explanation: "Glimrende" means "excellent". It comes from "at glimre" (to shine). To say things are going excellently, say: "Det går glimrende" (It is going excellently).

sentence.da: Du har lavet et **glimrende** stykke arbejde.
sentence.en: You have done an excellent piece of work.

global.explanation: "Global" means "global". It comes from "en globus" (a globe). The opposite is "lokal" (local). For example, "en lokal avis" (a local newspaper).

sentence.da: Klimaet er en **global** udfordring, ikke kun en dansk.
sentence.en: The climate is a global challenge, not only a Danish one.

global opvarmning.explanation: "Global opvarmning" means "global warming". "Opvarmning" comes from "at varme op" (to warm up), where "op" means "up". For example, "Jeg varmer maden op" (I warm up the food).

sentence.da: **Global opvarmning** får isen ved polerne til at smelte.
sentence.en: Global warming makes the ice at the poles melt.

gluten.explanation: "Gluten" means "gluten". To say a food has none, add "-fri" (free): "Brødet er glutenfrit" (The bread is gluten-free).

sentence.da: Der er **gluten** i hvedebrød.
sentence.en: There is gluten in wheat bread.

glutenfri.explanation: "Glutenfri" means "gluten-free". It is built from "gluten" and "fri" (free). The part "fri" also appears in "alkoholfri" (alcohol-free). For example, "alkoholfri øl" (alcohol-free beer).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser kun **glutenfri** pasta.
sentence.en: I only eat gluten-free pasta.

glæde.explanation: "Glæde" means "joy". To say you look forward to something, use "at glæde sig" (to look forward): "Jeg glæder mig til ferien" (I am looking forward to the vacation). To say you do something gladly, say "med glæde": "Det gør jeg med glæde" (I will do that gladly).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt lyste af **glæde**.
sentence.en: Her face lit up with joy.

glædelig jul.explanation: "Glædelig jul" means "merry Christmas". It is built from "glædelig" (merry) and "jul" (Christmas). To reply, say: "I lige måde" (Same to you). To add a New Year wish, say: "Glædelig jul og godt nytår" (Merry Christmas and happy New Year).

forms.en: Merry Christmas and happy New Year.

sentence.da: Vi har gaver og et juletræ. **Glædelig jul**!
sentence.en: We have presents and a Christmas tree. Merry Christmas!

glødende.explanation: "Glødende" means "glowing". It comes from "at gløde" (to glow). It also means "passionate". For example, "en glødende tilhænger" (a passionate supporter).

sentence.da: Smeden tog det **glødende** jern ud af ilden.
sentence.en: The blacksmith took the glowing iron out of the fire.

gløgg.explanation: "Gløgg" means "mulled wine". Spell it with "ø" and a double "g": "gløgg". In Denmark, people drink it at Christmas time together with "æbleskiver" (Danish pancake balls).

forms.en: mulled wine and Danish pancake balls

sentence.da: I december drikker mange varm **gløgg** for at holde varmen.
sentence.en: In December, many people drink hot mulled wine to keep warm.

gnaven.explanation: "Gnaven" means "grumpy". To describe someone's voice as grumpy, say: "Han har en gnaven stemme" (He has a grumpy voice).

sentence.da: Min bror er altid **gnaven**, når han er sulten.
sentence.en: My brother is always grumpy when he is hungry.

god.explanation: "God" means "good". To say something goes well, use "godt": "Det går godt" (It is going well). To wish someone a good weekend, say: "God weekend!" (Have a good weekend!)

sentence.da: Han hjælper altid. Han er en **god** ven.
sentence.en: He always helps. He is a good friend.

god appetit.explanation: "God appetit" means "enjoy your meal". To reply, say: "I lige måde" (Same to you). At the end of a meal, Danes thank the cook with "tak for mad" (thanks for the food), and the cook answers "velbekomme" (you are welcome).

sentence.da: Maden er klar. **God appetit**!
sentence.en: The food is ready. Enjoy your meal!

god bedring.explanation: "God bedring" means "get well soon". "Bedring" means "improvement", so you are wishing them a good recovery. To name the illness or injury, add "med" (with): "God bedring med foden" (Get well soon with your foot).

forms.en: Get well soon with your cold.

sentence.da: Du er syg? **God bedring**!
sentence.en: Are you sick? Get well soon!

god fornøjelse.explanation: "God fornøjelse" means "enjoy". It is built from "god" (good) and "en fornøjelse" (a pleasure). To name the event, add "med" (with): "God fornøjelse med koncerten" (Enjoy the concert).

sentence.da: Vi skal i teatret. **God fornøjelse**!
sentence.en: We are going to the theater. Enjoy!

god påske.explanation: "God påske" means "happy Easter". In Denmark, the Easter holiday has its own lunch, "påskefrokost" (Easter lunch). For example, "Vi spiser påskefrokost hos mormor" (We are eating Easter lunch at grandmother's).

sentence.da: Vi ses efter ferien. **God påske**!
sentence.en: See you after the holiday. Happy Easter!

god til.explanation: "God til" means "good at". To name a subject, put it right after "god til": "god til matematik" (good at math). To name an action, put "at" and the action word after it: "god til at synge" (good at singing).

forms.da: Jeg er god til at lave mad.
Han er ikke god til sport.
forms.en: He is not good at sports.

sentence.da: Han er **god til** at spille fodbold.
sentence.en: He is good at playing soccer.

god tur.explanation: "God tur" means "have a good trip". The word "tur" also appears in "en cykeltur" (a bike ride). For example, "Vi tager på cykeltur" (We are going on a bike ride).

forms.en: Have a good trip to Copenhagen.

sentence.da: Vi tager af sted nu. — **God tur**!
sentence.en: We are leaving now. — Have a good trip!

god weekend.explanation: "God weekend" means "have a good weekend". To ask on Monday how it went, say: "Havde du en god weekend?" (Did you have a good weekend?)

forms.en: Have a good weekend, all of you.

sentence.da: Vi ses på mandag. **God weekend**!
sentence.en: See you on Monday. Have a good weekend!

godaften.explanation: "Godaften" means "good evening". Write it as one word, not "god aften". When you go to bed, say "godnat" (good night) instead: "Godnat, mor!" (Good night, Mom!)

sentence.da: **Godaften**, Peter! Hvordan har du det?
sentence.en: Good evening, Peter! How are you?

goddag.explanation: "Goddag" means "good day". It is formal. With friends, say "hej" (hi) instead: "Hej, Peter!" (Hi, Peter!)

sentence.da: **Goddag**, jeg hedder Peter.
sentence.en: Hello, my name is Peter.

godhed.explanation: "En godhed" means "goodness". It is built from "god" (good) and "-hed" (-ness). The ending "-hed" also appears in "frihed" (freedom). For example, "Vi har frihed" (We have freedom).

sentence.da: Alle kender hende for hendes **godhed** mod dyr.
sentence.en: Everyone knows her for her goodness toward animals.

godmorgen.explanation: "Godmorgen" means "good morning". It is built from "god" (good) and "en morgen" (a morning). Write it as one word, not "god morgen".

sentence.da: **Godmorgen**! Har du sovet godt?
sentence.en: Good morning! Did you sleep well?

godnat.explanation: "Godnat" means "good night". To greet someone you meet in the evening, use "godaften" (good evening) instead: "Godaften, Peter!" (Good evening, Peter!)

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i seng. **Godnat**!
sentence.en: I am tired and going to bed. Good night!

godt nytår.explanation: "Godt nytår" means "happy New Year". It is built from "godt" (good) and "nytår" (New Year). English speakers may say "god nytår", but the Danish greeting uses "godt".

forms.en: Happy New Year to you all.

sentence.da: Det er midnat. **Godt nytår**!
sentence.en: It is midnight. Happy New Year!

golf.explanation: "Golf" means "golf". To name the place where it is played, add "bane" (course): "en golfbane" (a golf course). To say you are going there, say: "Vi går på golfbanen" (We are going to the golf course).

sentence.da: Jeg spiller **golf** på en grøn bane.
sentence.en: I play golf on a green course.

grader.explanation: "Grader" means "degrees". To say it is below zero, put "minus" before the number: "Det er minus to grader" (It is minus two degrees).

sentence.da: Der er kun fem **grader** udenfor.
sentence.en: It is only five degrees outside.

gradvist.explanation: "Gradvist" means "gradually". To describe a change, use "gradvis" (gradual): "en gradvis ændring" (a gradual change).

sentence.da: Isen smelter ikke på én dag, men **gradvist** over flere uger.
sentence.en: The ice does not melt in one day, but gradually over several weeks.

gratis.explanation: "Gratis" means "free", as in costing no money. Do not mix it up with "fri", which means off from work or school. For example, "Jeg har fri i dag" (I have the day off today).

sentence.da: Du skal ikke betale. Det er **gratis**.
sentence.en: You do not have to pay. It is free.

grillkul.explanation: "Grillkul" means "charcoal". It is built from "grill" (barbecue) and "kul" (coal). To say you light the barbecue, say: "Vi tænder grillen" (We light the grill).

sentence.da: Vi lægger **grillkul** i grillen og tænder det.
sentence.en: We put charcoal in the grill and light it.

grim.explanation: "Grim" means "ugly". It also means "nasty". For example, "grimt vejr" (nasty weather) and "et grimt ord" (a nasty word). It is very rude to say about a person: "Du er grim" (You are ugly).

sentence.da: Bygningen er **grim** og ikke smuk.
sentence.en: The building is ugly and not beautiful.

grov.explanation: "Grov" means "coarse". To say a mistake is serious, use it before "fejl" (mistake): "en grov fejl" (a serious mistake). A common word partner is sand. For example, "grov sand" (coarse sand).

sentence.da: Han fortalte en **grov** vittighed, og ingen grinede.
sentence.en: He told a rude joke, and nobody laughed.

grundig.explanation: "Grundig" means "thorough". It comes from "grund" (bottom, foundation). To describe a check of every detail, put it before "kontrol" (check): "en grundig kontrol" (a thorough check).

sentence.da: Lægen lavede en **grundig** undersøgelse og tog mange prøver.
sentence.en: The doctor did a thorough examination and took many samples.

grundigt.explanation: "Grundigt" means "thoroughly". It comes from "grundig" (thorough). To say something was examined in detail, put it after the verb: "Politiet undersøgte sagen grundigt" (The police investigated the case thoroughly).

sentence.da: Jeg læste kontrakten **grundigt** og fandt tre fejl.
sentence.en: I read the contract thoroughly and found three mistakes.

grundlovsdag.explanation: "Grundlovsdag" means "Constitution Day", 5 June, the day in 1849 when Denmark's first constitution was signed. It is built from grundlov (constitution) and dag (day).

sentence.da: På **grundlovsdag** holder politikere ofte taler om demokrati.
sentence.en: On Constitution Day, politicians often give speeches about democracy.

grundlæggende.explanation: "Grundlæggende" means "basic". It is built from "grund" (foundation) and "at lægge" (to lay). To say something is wrong at its core: "Det er grundlæggende forkert" (It is fundamentally wrong).

sentence.da: Alle mennesker har et **grundlæggende** behov for mad og vand.
sentence.en: All people have a basic need for food and water.

grå.explanation: "Grå" means "gray". To describe a dull, cloudy day, use it before "dag" (day): "en grå dag" (a gray day). To say someone's hair has turned gray: "Hun har grå hår" (She has gray hair).

sentence.da: Himlen er **grå** og ikke blå.
sentence.en: The sky is gray and not blue.

grådig.explanation: "Grådig" means "greedy". To say what someone is greedy for, add "efter" (after) and the thing: "grådig efter penge" (greedy for money).

sentence.da: Han er **grådig** og tager altid den største kage.
sentence.en: He is greedy and always takes the biggest cake.

gråvejr.explanation: "Gråvejr" means "gray weather". It is built from "grå" (gray) and "vejr" (weather). To say you are fed up with it: "Jeg er træt af gråvejr" (I am tired of gray weather).

sentence.da: Der er **gråvejr** og grå himmel.
sentence.en: It is gray weather with a gray sky.

grækenland.explanation: "Grækenland" means "Greece". It is built from græker (a Greek person) and land (country). The word "land" ends many country names. For example, "Tyskland" (Germany) and "Irland" (Ireland).

sentence.da: Athen er en by i **Grækenland**.
sentence.en: Athens is a city in Greece.

grænseløs.explanation: "Grænseløs" means "boundless". The ending "-løs" means "without", so "grænse" (border) plus "-løs" is "without a border". The same ending is in "hjælpeløs" (helpless).

sentence.da: Børns fantasi er **grænseløs**, og alt kan ske.
sentence.en: Children's imagination is boundless, and anything can happen.

græs.explanation: "Græs" means "grass". To say you mow the lawn, use "at slå græs" (literally, "to hit grass"): "Jeg skal slå græs i dag" (I am going to mow the lawn today).

sentence.da: Koen æder **græs** på marken.
sentence.en: The cow eats grass in the field.

græsk.explanation: "Græsk" means "Greek". To say a food comes from Greece, put it before the noun: "græsk salat" (Greek salad).

sentence.da: Hun er fra Grækenland og taler **græsk**.
sentence.en: She is from Greece and speaks Greek.

grød.explanation: "En grød" means "a porridge". Add the grain in front to name the kind: "havregrød" (oat porridge).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser varm **grød** med mælk til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I eat warm porridge with milk for breakfast.

grøn.explanation: "Grøn" means "green". It also means eco-friendly. For example, "grøn energi" (green energy). Vegetables are "grøntsager" (literally, "green things").

sentence.da: Bilen er **grøn** som græs.
sentence.en: The car is green like grass.

grønland.explanation: "Grønland" means "Greenland". It is built from grøn (green) and land (country), so literally green land. Many country names end in "land". For example, "Tyskland" (Germany) and "Irland" (Ireland).

sentence.da: **Grønland** er en stor ø med is.
sentence.en: Greenland is a big island with ice.

grønlandsk.explanation: "Grønlandsk" means "Greenlandic". It is built from "Grønland" (Greenland). To say a food comes from there: "grønlandsk mad" (Greenlandic food). In Danish the first letter is "g", not "G" as in "Greenlandic".

sentence.da: På Grønland taler de fleste **grønlandsk**, og mange kan også dansk.
sentence.en: In Greenland, most people speak Greenlandic, and many also know Danish.

grøntsager.explanation: "Grøntsager" means "vegetables". It is built from "grønt" (greens) and "sager" (things). In a shop, you find them in the section called "frugt og grønt" (fruit and vegetables).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gulerødder og andre **grøntsager**.
sentence.en: I eat carrots and other vegetables.

gudskelov.explanation: "Gudskelov" means "Thank God". It is short for "Gud ske lov" (God be praised). To say you are relieved after a scare: "Er alle okay?" "Ja, gudskelov." (Is everyone okay? Yes, thank God.)

sentence.da: **Gudskelov** kom ingen til skade i ulykken.
sentence.en: Thank God, no one was hurt in the accident.

gul.explanation: "Gul" means "yellow". A traditional Danish soup is called "gule ærter" (yellow peas).

sentence.da: Solen er **gul** og himlen blå.
sentence.en: The sun is yellow and the sky is blue.

guld.explanation: "Guld" means "gold". To tell someone they are a great help, say: "Du er guld værd" (literally, "You are worth gold").

sentence.da: Ringen er lavet af **guld**.
sentence.en: The ring is made of gold.

gummi.explanation: "Gummi" means "rubber". To name a chewy sweet, it also begins a word: "gummibjørne" (gummy bears).

sentence.da: Støvler af **gummi** holder fødderne tørre.
sentence.en: Boots made of rubber keep your feet dry.

gylden.explanation: "Gylden" means "golden". To say a ring is made of real gold, use "guld" (gold) instead: "Hun har en guldring" (She has a gold ring).

sentence.da: Solen var **gylden** over havet.
sentence.en: The sun was golden over the sea.

gyldig.explanation: "Gyldig" means "valid". To say until when, use "til" (until): "Kørekortet er gyldigt til 2030" (The driver's license is valid until 2030).

sentence.da: Billetten er **gyldig** i to timer efter købet.
sentence.en: The ticket is valid for two hours after the purchase.

gymnastik.explanation: "Gymnastik" means "gymnastics". The same word is used for simple exercises you do for your body: "Jeg laver gymnastik hver morgen" (I do exercises every morning).

sentence.da: Børnene går til **gymnastik** to gange om ugen.
sentence.en: The children go to gymnastics twice a week.

gådefuld.explanation: "Gådefuld" means "mysterious". It is built from "gåde" (riddle) and "-fuld" (full of). The same ending is in "smertefuld" (painful).

sentence.da: Hendes svar var kort og **gådefuld**.
sentence.en: Her answer was short and mysterious.

gær.explanation: "Gær" means "yeast". To give a recipe step, say: "Rør gæren ud i lunkent vand" (Stir the yeast into lukewarm water).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger **gær**, når jeg bager brød.
sentence.en: I use yeast when I bake bread.

gødning.explanation: "En gødning" means "a fertilizer". To name the kind, put a word in front: "kunstgødning" (artificial fertilizer).

sentence.da: Landmanden spreder **gødning** på marken for at hjælpe planterne.
sentence.en: The farmer spreads fertilizer on the field to help the plants.

gør det selv.explanation: "Gør det selv" means "do it yourself". It is built from "gør" (do), "det" (it) and "selv" (yourself). The word "selv" stays the same for every person. For example, "Vi gør det selv" (We do it ourselves).

sentence.da: Jeg hjælper dig ikke. **Gør det selv**!
sentence.en: I will not help you. Do it yourself!
